Scientific Officer Recruitment Examination
About the Examination

The Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC) conducts its nationwide examination for the recruitment of Scientific Officers (Group 'A' post) for various units of the Department of Atomic Energy (DAE). This is one of the most prestigious gateways for engineering graduates to embark on a career at the forefront of nuclear science, research, and technology in India. The recruitment is done through two main schemes: OCES and DGFS.
📜 The Schemes: OCES & DGFS
Selected candidates are admitted into one of the two training programs, which are the cornerstone for grooming the next generation of scientists and engineers for the DAE.

OCES (Orientation Course for Engineering Graduates and Science Postgraduates): This is a one-year training program conducted at various BARC Training Schools located across India. OCES Trainee Scientific Officers (TSOs) who successfully complete the program are appointed as Scientific Officers 'C' in one of the DAE units.

DGFS (DAE Graduate Fellowship Scheme for Engineering Graduates): This is a two-year program for candidates who want to pursue an M.Tech. degree while receiving a stipend from DAE. Fellows complete their M.Tech. at select premier institutes (like certain IITs/NITIE) and are then posted as Scientific Officers in DAE.
🎯 The Philosophy Behind the Selection

Unlike many other PSU exams that test a wide range of general and technical subjects, the BARC selection process is intensely focused on evaluating the depth of fundamental knowledge in a candidate's core engineering discipline. It seeks individuals who possess:
Strong Conceptual Clarity: The ability to explain core engineering principles from the ground up.
Analytical & Problem-Solving Skills: The capacity to apply theoretical knowledge to solve complex, practical problems.
Research Aptitude: A curious and innovative mindset suitable for a research and development organization.
Sustained Academic Excellence: A consistent and strong academic record, reflecting a solid foundation.
🪜 The Two-Stage Selection Process
The BARC selection process is a two-step funnel designed to identify candidates with genuine technical prowess.

Stage 1: Screening Test (The Gateway): This is a shortlisting stage. Candidates can be shortlisted for the final interview based on their performance in either an online, discipline-specific examination conducted by BARC, or through their valid GATE (Graduate Aptitude Test in Engineering) score . This stage serves only to filter the candidates for the crucial next step.

Stage 2: Selection Interview (The Ultimate Test): This is the final and most decisive stage. Candidates shortlisted from Stage 1 are called for a personal interview in Mumbai. The interview, conducted by a panel of senior DAE scientists, is a purely technical and rigorous assessment of the candidate's subject knowledge. The final selection is based solely on performance in this interview.
Typical Timeline (Indicative)

The BARC recruitment cycle is relatively short and efficient, typically concluding within 6-7 months from notification to the commencement of the course. Understanding this schedule is vital for aspirants.
⚠️ Disclaimer: These are approximate timelines based on past trends. Always refer to the official BARC recruitment portal for the exact dates of the current cycle.
Phase 1: Notification & Application (December - January)

Late December / Early January: The official notification is released on the BARC online examination portal (barconlineexam.in). It contains details on eligible disciplines, vacancies, eligibility, and important dates.

January - Early February: The online application window opens and typically remains active for about a month. Candidates must fill the form, choose their shortlisting method (Online Exam, GATE Score, or both), and pay the fee.
Phase 2: Admit Card Release (Late February)
Approximately 2-3 weeks before the exam window , BARC releases the admit cards for candidates who opted for the online examination.
Phase 3: Online Examination (March)
The BARC online computer-based test is conducted over a window of a few days (e.g., a weekend) at various centers across India. Each candidate is assigned a specific date and time slot.
Phase 4: Shortlisting for Interview (March - April)
Late March: Results of the online examination are declared.
Early April: A consolidated list of candidates shortlisted for the interview is released. This list includes candidates selected via the online exam and those selected based on their GATE scores.
Phase 5: Interview Slot Booking (April)
Shortlisted candidates are required to log in to the portal and book their preferred date for the selection interview from the available slots.
Phase 6: Selection Interviews (May - June)
The personal interviews are conducted over several weeks, primarily at the BARC campus in Mumbai.
Phase 7: Final Result Declaration (Late June / Early July)
A final merit list of selected candidates is published, based entirely on their performance in the interview. Selected candidates are notified about their allotted scheme (OCES or DGFS).
Phase 8: Commencement of Program (August)
The Orientation Course (OCES) typically begins in the first week of August at the BARC Training Schools. DGFS fellows join their respective M.Tech. programs.
Eligibility Criteria
Candidates must strictly fulfill the eligibility criteria related to nationality, age, and educational qualifications to be considered for the BARC Scientific Officer position.
⚠️ Note: The official notification for the current examination year is the final authority on all eligibility criteria.
🌍 1. Nationality
The candidate must be a citizen of India .
🎂 2. Age Limit
The age is calculated as of the 1st of August of the examination year. The general age limits are:
Note: Physically Challenged persons of all categories are eligible for age relaxation of 10 years.
🎓 3. Educational Qualification
Qualifying Degree: A B.E. / B.Tech. / B.Sc. (Engineering) / 5-year Integrated M.Tech. degree is required.
Minimum Marks: Candidates must have a minimum of 60% aggregate marks (or equivalent CGPA) in their qualifying degree.

Final Year Students: Students in the final year of their B.E./B.Tech. or Integrated M.Tech. are eligible to apply, provided they can produce their final results by the specified date in the notification.
🛠️ 4. Eligible Engineering Disciplines
Candidates must have a degree in one of the following (or equivalent) engineering disciplines:
The list of eligible disciplines and their equivalent branches is detailed in the official notification.
GATE Score Eligibility
Candidates can also be shortlisted based on their GATE score. The requirements are:
A valid GATE score from the current or previous year, as specified in the notification.
The GATE paper must be in the same engineering discipline as the qualifying degree.
Selection Process & Exam Pattern
The BARC selection is a two-stage process: a screening stage to shortlist candidates, followed by a selection interview which is the final determinant of merit.
🎯 Stage 1: Screening for Interview
Shortlisting for the interview is done through two independent channels. Candidates can opt for either or both.
BARC conducts its own discipline-specific computer-based test.
Candidates can also apply on the basis of their valid GATE score .
BARC sets a separate cut-off for each engineering discipline to shortlist candidates directly for the interview.
Applying through GATE is a separate shortlisting channel and does not depend on the online exam.
Note: The screening exam score or GATE score is only for shortlisting and has NO weightage in the final selection.
🗣️ Stage 2: Selection Interview
This is the final and most crucial stage. The interview is a rigorous test of a candidate's technical acumen.
Nature of Interview: It is purely technical, focusing on the fundamental concepts of the candidate's engineering discipline. There are typically no HR or general knowledge questions.
Interview Panel: The board consists of senior scientists and experts from DAE.

Evaluation Criteria: The panel assesses the depth of understanding, analytical ability, and problem-solving skills. Candidates are expected to derive equations and explain concepts from first principles.
Location: Interviews are primarily conducted at the BARC campus in Mumbai.
📊 Final Merit List
Final selection is based solely on performance in the personal interview .
Application Workflow
The application for BARC OCES/DGFS is a completely online process. Candidates must be careful while filling out the form as details submitted are final.
📝 Stage 1: Registration
Visit the official BARC recruitment portal: barconlineexam.in .
Register by providing basic details like name, date of birth, email ID, and mobile number.
A login ID and password will be generated and sent to your registered email/mobile.
✍️ Stage 2: Filling the Application Form
Log in with your credentials and fill in the application form.

Signature: On white paper with a black pen. (Format: JPG, Size: 10KB - 20KB).
💳 Stage 4: Fee Payment
Application Fee: ₹500 (Rupees Five Hundred). This is non-refundable.

Payment Mode: The fee must be paid online through Net Banking, Credit Card, or Debit Card.
✅ Stage 5: Final Submission
Review the entire application form carefully before final submission. No changes are allowed after submission.

Syllabus

The syllabus for the BARC Online Examination is broadly based on the curriculum of the qualifying B.E. / B.Tech. degree for the respective engineering discipline. It is essentially equivalent to the GATE syllabus for that branch.
🖥️ Computer Science & Engineering (CS)
Engineering Mathematics: Discrete Mathematics, Linear Algebra, Calculus, Probability and Statistics.
Digital Logic: Boolean algebra, Combinational and sequential circuits, Minimization.
Computer Organization and Architecture: Machine instructions and addressing modes, ALU, Data-path and control unit, Memory hierarchy, I/O interface.
Programming and Data Structures: Programming in C, Recursion, Arrays, Stacks, Queues, Linked lists, Trees, Graphs, Hashing.
Algorithms: Searching, Sorting, Asymptotic notations, Graph traversals, Dynamic programming, Greedy algorithms.
Theory of Computation: Regular expressions and finite automata, Context-free grammars and push-down automata, Turing machines.
Compiler Design: Lexical analysis, Parsing, Syntax-directed translation, Runtime environments.
Operating System: Processes, Threads, CPU scheduling, Memory management, File systems, Concurrency and Synchronization.
Databases: ER-model, Relational model, SQL, Integrity constraints, Normal forms, Transactions and concurrency control.
Computer Networks: ISO/OSI stack, LAN technologies (Ethernet), TCP/UDP, IP(v4/v6), Routing algorithms, Application layer protocols.
⚙️ Mechanical Engineering (ME)
Engineering Mathematics: Linear Algebra, Calculus, Differential Equations, Probability & Statistics, Numerical Methods.
Applied Mechanics and Design: Engineering Mechanics, Mechanics of Materials, Theory of Machines, Vibrations, Machine Design.
Fluid Mechanics and Thermal Sciences: Fluid Mechanics, Heat-Transfer, Thermodynamics, Applications (Power Engineering, IC Engines, Refrigeration).

Materials, Manufacturing and Industrial Engineering: Engineering Materials, Casting, Forming and Joining Processes, Machining, Metrology and Inspection, Production Planning and Control, Operations Research.
💡 Electrical Engineering (EE)
Engineering Mathematics: Linear Algebra, Calculus, Differential Equations, Complex variables, Probability and Statistics.
Electric Circuits: Network elements, Network solution methods, AC analysis, Transient and steady-state analysis.
Electromagnetic Fields: Maxwell's equations, Transmission lines, Waveguides.
Signals and Systems: LTI systems, Fourier Series, Fourier Transform, Laplace Transform, Z-Transform.
Electrical Machines: Single phase transformers, three phase transformers, DC machines, synchronous machines, three phase induction motors.
Power Systems: Power generation concepts, AC and DC transmission concepts, Economic load dispatch, Fault analysis, Stability analysis.
Control Systems: Mathematical modeling and representation of systems, Feedback principle, Stability analysis, Root locus, Bode plot.
Electrical and Electronic Measurements: Bridges and potentiometers, Measurement of voltage, current, power, energy and power factor.
Analog and Digital Electronics: Diode circuits, BJT and MOSFET amplifiers, Operational amplifiers, Combinational and sequential logic circuits.
Power Electronics: Static V-I characteristics of semiconductor devices, DC to DC conversion, AC to DC conversion, DC to AC conversion.
📡 Electronics & Communication Engineering (EC)
Engineering Mathematics: Linear Algebra, Calculus, Differential Equations, Vector Analysis, Complex Analysis, Probability and Statistics.
Networks, Signals and Systems: Circuit analysis, Time and frequency domain analysis of continuous and discrete-time signals, LTI Systems.
Electronic Devices: Energy bands in intrinsic and extrinsic semiconductors, Carrier transport, P-N Junction, BJT, MOS, LED, photo-diode and solar cell.
Analog Circuits: Diode circuits, BJT and MOSFET amplifiers, Operational amplifier circuits, Filters, Oscillators.
Digital Circuits: Number representations and computer arithmetic, Combinational and sequential circuits, Data converters (ADC, DAC), Microprocessor (8085).
Control Systems: Basic control system components, Feedback principle, Stability analysis (Routh-Hurwitz, Nyquist, Bode).
Communications: Analog modulation (AM, FM, PM), Digital communications (PCM, ASK, FSK, PSK), Information theory and coding.
Electromagnetics: Maxwell’s equations, Plane waves, Transmission lines, Waveguides, Antennas.
🏗️ Civil Engineering (CE)
Engineering Mathematics: Linear Algebra, Calculus, Ordinary and Partial Differential Equations, Probability & Statistics, Numerical Methods.
Structural Engineering: Engineering Mechanics, Solid Mechanics, Structural Analysis, Concrete Structures, Steel Structures.
Geotechnical Engineering: Soil Mechanics, Foundation Engineering.
Water Resources Engineering: Fluid Mechanics, Hydrology, Irrigation, Open Channel Flow, Pipeline systems.
Environmental Engineering: Water and wastewater quality and treatment, Air pollution, Municipal solid wastes.
Transportation Engineering: Highway planning and geometric design, Traffic engineering.
Geomatics Engineering: Principles of surveying, Levelling, Theodolite traversing.
Frequently Asked Questions
❓ Regarding Eligibility & Application

Can I apply in my final year of B.Tech.? Yes. Final year students are eligible to apply. However, they must obtain their final degree results with the required percentage by the date specified in the official notification.
Is there a minimum percentage required in B.Tech.? Yes. A minimum of 60% aggregate marks (or equivalent CGPA) is mandatory in the qualifying degree.

Can I apply through both GATE and the online exam? Yes. You can and should apply through both channels if you have a valid GATE score. This maximizes your chances of getting shortlisted for the interview as they are treated as separate shortlisting streams.
❓ Regarding the Examination
Is a calculator allowed in the online exam? Yes. A virtual scientific calculator is provided on the computer screen during the examination. Personal calculators are not allowed.
Is there negative marking? Yes. For every correct answer, 3 marks are awarded, and for every incorrect answer, 1 mark is deducted.
What is the difficulty level of the BARC online exam? The level is generally considered to be on par with or slightly easier than the GATE exam. It focuses strongly on fundamental concepts.
❓ Regarding the Interview & Selection

How important is the selection interview? It is the most important stage. The final selection is based 100% on your performance in the interview. Your online exam score or GATE score has no weightage in the final merit list.
Where are the interviews conducted? The selection interviews are conducted primarily at the BARC campus in Anushaktinagar, Mumbai .

What is the difference between OCES and DGFS? OCES is a one-year orientation/training program at a BARC training school, after which you are posted as a Scientific Officer. DGFS is a two-year fellowship where you complete your M.Tech. from a premier institute (like IITs) with a DAE stipend, and then join as a Scientific Officer. The choice between OCES and DGFS is offered based on merit after the final results.

BPSC Combined Competitive Examination
About the Examination

The Bihar Public Service Commission (BPSC) Combined Competitive Examination (CCE) is the state-level examination for recruitment to various civil services and posts within the Government of Bihar. It is a comprehensive, multi-stage process designed to select the state's future administrative leaders. Regarded as one of the most prestigious state civil services exams in India, it serves as the gateway to a career in public service that directly impacts the governance and development of Bihar.
📜 The Philosophy Behind the Examination

The BPSC CCE is engineered to assess more than just rote memorization. Its core philosophy is to identify individuals who possess a potent combination of intellectual depth, analytical acuity, ethical integrity, and a profound understanding of the state's socio-economic landscape . The examination seeks to evaluate a candidate's:
Critical Assimilation: The ability to understand complex information from diverse fields, filter out noise, and grasp the core issues relevant to the state and nation.
Balance of Judgment: The capacity to form reasoned opinions, consider multiple perspectives, and make sound, unbiased judgments.
Intellectual and Moral Integrity: A strong ethical compass and the courage to uphold constitutional and administrative values.
Leadership and Social Cohesion: The potential to lead and work collaboratively to solve pressing societal problems at the state level.
Awareness and Curiosity: A deep and abiding interest in local, state, national, and international affairs.
🏛️ The Services at Stake
Successful candidates are allocated to various state-level services based on their rank and preferences. These services form the backbone of the state's administrative machinery.
Key Group 'A' & 'B' Services:
and several others, including posts like Municipal Executive Officer, Revenue Officer, Block Panchayat Raj Officer, etc.
🪜 The Three-Tiered Selection Gauntlet

The CCE is a multi-layered process where each stage serves as a progressively finer filter to identify the most suitable candidates. The entire cycle, from notification to the final result, spans over a year.

Stage 1: Preliminary Examination (The Filter): This is an objective-type (Multiple Choice Questions) screening test. Its primary role is to eliminate non-serious candidates and select a manageable number for the Mains exam. It tests the breadth of a candidate's knowledge. Crucially, the marks from this stage are not counted for the final merit list. It is a pass/fail gateway to the next level.

Stage 2: Main Examination (The Crucible): Candidates who clear the Prelims undertake the Main Examination, a descriptive (written) exam that is the real test of intellectual depth and analytical skill. Spread over five papers (including qualifying ones), it evaluates a candidate's ability to articulate nuanced arguments and structure comprehensive answers. The marks from the Main Examination are the most significant component of the final score.

Stage 3: Personality Test (The Final Appraisal): The final stage is an interview conducted by a board of distinguished experts at the BPSC headquarters in Patna. The board, having access to the candidate's Detailed Application Form, assesses their personality, mental alertness, leadership qualities, and suitability for a high-stakes career in the state's public administration.
🏆 The Final Verdict: Merit and Allocation

The final merit list is prepared based on the total marks obtained in the Main Examination (900 marks) and the Personality Test (120 marks) , for a grand total of 1020 marks. Based on their final rank, the preferences for services submitted by them, their category, and the vacancies available, candidates are allocated a service. This final allocation marks the successful culmination of one of the most demanding journeys in the Bihar state examination landscape.
Typical Timeline (Indicative)

The BPSC CCE schedule can vary, but it generally follows a year-long cycle. Understanding this timeline is crucial for strategic planning and sustained preparation. The following is a typical, indicative schedule based on recent trends.
⚠️ Disclaimer: These timelines are based on past trends. Always refer to the official BPSC calendar and notifications for the specific year for exact dates.
Phase 1: Notification & Application (June - August)

June / July: The official notification for the Combined Competitive Examination is released by BPSC on its website (bpsc.bih.nic.in). This document contains all essential details: vacancy numbers, eligibility, syllabus, and exam rules.

July - August: The online application window opens and typically remains active for about a month. This process involves a one-time registration (OTR) and filling out the application form. Aspirants must be careful while filling in details and uploading documents.
Phase 2: Preliminary Examination (September - October)
September: Approximately 2-3 weeks before the exam date, BPSC releases the e-Admit Card. Candidates must download and print it.
Late September / Early October: The Preliminary Exam is conducted on a single day. It consists of one paper of General Studies.
Phase 3: Prelims Result & Mains Application (November - December)
November: The results of the Preliminary Examination are typically declared within 4-6 weeks of the exam date. BPSC releases a list of the roll numbers of qualified candidates.

November - December: Shortly after the Prelims result, the qualified candidates are required to fill out the Detailed Application Form (DAF) for the Mains exam. This form collects detailed information and is also where candidates indicate their optional subject.
Phase 4: Main Examination (January - February)
December / January: Admit cards for the Main Examination are released for candidates who have successfully submitted their DAF.
January / February: The Main Examination is a descriptive (written) test conducted over 3-4 days.
Phase 5: Mains Result & Interview Schedule (May - June)
May / June: The results of the Main Examination are usually announced about 3 to 4 months after the exam. A list of candidates who have qualified for the Personality Test (Interview) is published.
Phase 6: Personality Tests (Interviews) (July - August)
The Personality Tests (Interviews) typically commence a few weeks after the Mains results are declared.
Candidates are summoned to the BPSC office in Patna in batches. The interview schedule is spread over several weeks.
Phase 7: Final Result Declaration (August - September)

This is the culmination of the entire process. The final merit list, based on the combined scores of the Main Examination and the Personality Test, is declared, usually within a few weeks of the conclusion of the last interview.
Eligibility Criteria

Before embarking on the rigorous journey of BPSC preparation, every aspirant must meticulously verify their eligibility. The criteria set by the Bihar Public Service Commission are strict and non-negotiable. Eligibility is primarily determined by four key parameters: Nationality, Age Limit, Educational Qualification, and Number of Attempts.
⚠️ Note: The details provided here are based on prevailing rules. These are subject to change, and the official BPSC notification for the current examination year is the ultimate authority.
🌍 1. Nationality
A candidate must be a citizen of India to be eligible for the BPSC CCE.
🎂 2. Age Limit
The age of a candidate is calculated as of a specific cut-off date, which is typically the 1st of August of the examination year. The age limits vary depending on the post and category.
Minimum Age: 20, 21, or 22 years , depending on the service/post. (e.g., 20 years for Dy. SP, 22 years for others like SDM).
Maximum Age: The upper age limit varies by category.
BPSC provides relaxations in the upper age limit for candidates from different categories:
Note: Candidates must refer to the official notification for post-specific age requirements and detailed relaxation norms.
🎓 3. Educational Qualification
The minimum educational requirement is straightforward:
A candidate must hold a Bachelor's degree (Graduate) or an equivalent qualification from a recognized University.

Final-Year Students: Candidates who have appeared or intend to appear for their final degree examination and are awaiting results are also eligible to apply. However, they must have passed the exam by the time of filling the Mains application form.
✍️ 4. Number of Attempts
The number of times a candidate can appear for the examination is limited. Appearing in the Preliminary Exam is counted as an attempt.

Note: The attempt limit policy has changed over time. As per the latest rules, there is no separate attempt limit for most categories; eligibility is determined by the age limit. Always verify with the latest notification.
Stages, Exam Pattern & Marking Scheme

The BPSC CCE is a meticulously designed three-stage process. Each stage has a distinct purpose and format. A thorough understanding of this pattern is the first step toward building a successful preparation strategy.
🎯 Stage 1: Preliminary Examination (Objective Type)
The primary purpose of the Prelims is to screen candidates for the Main Examination. The marks obtained in this stage are not counted for the final merit list.
Objective Format: The paper consists of Multiple Choice Questions (MCQs).
Negative Marking: There is a penalty for incorrect answers. For each wrong answer, one-third (1/3rd) of the marks assigned to that question will be deducted.
No CSAT Paper: Unlike UPSC, BPSC Prelims consists of only one General Studies paper.
Merit Calculation: The cut-off for qualifying for the Main Examination is determined solely based on the marks scored in this paper.
📝 Stage 2: Main Examination (Descriptive + Objective)
This stage is the core of the selection process. The marks obtained here are the primary determinant of a candidate's final rank. It consists of 5 papers.
Candidates must clear these papers to have their other Mains papers evaluated.
Failing to secure the qualifying marks in these papers will lead to disqualification.
The sum of marks from these three papers determines the written score for the final merit list.
🗣️ Stage 3: Personality Test (Interview)
The final stage is a face-to-face interview with the BPSC board. It is an assessment of personality, suitability for public service, and mental calibre.
Maximum Marks: 120 Marks
Basis of Interview: The conversation is largely guided by the candidate's Detailed Application Form (DAF), covering their hobbies, academic background, work experience, and knowledge of Bihar.
Qualities Assessed: The board evaluates mental alertness, leadership qualities, clear and logical exposition, balance of judgment, and intellectual and moral integrity.
📊 Final Rank Calculation
The final merit list is prepared based on the cumulative score of the Main Examination and the Personality Test.
Main Exam (Written Merit Papers) Marks: 900 + Personality Test (Interview) Marks: 120 = Grand Total: 1020 Marks
Application Workflow

The application process for the BPSC CCE is conducted exclusively online through the official BPSC website (onlinebpsc.bihar.gov.in). It is a meticulous process that requires careful attention to detail. Any error can lead to the rejection of the application.
📝 Stage 1: One-Time Registration (OTR)
Before filling out the application form, a candidate must complete the One-Time Registration. As the name suggests, this is a one-time activity.
Purpose: The OTR platform saves a candidate's basic personal information, which is used for all BPSC exam applications.
Information Required: You will need to provide your name, parents' names, date of birth, a valid mobile number, a valid email ID, Aadhaar number, and other basic details.
Verification: The mobile number and email ID are verified through OTPs. It is crucial to use an active and personal number and email.
✍️ Stage 2: Filling the Examination Application Form
Once your OTR is complete, you can log in and apply for the Combined Competitive (Preliminary) Examination.
1. Fee Payment:
Amount: Application fee is typically ₹600 for General category candidates.
Exemptions: The fee is reduced to ₹150 for SC/ST candidates of Bihar, permanent residents of Bihar (all categories of women), and persons with disabilities (40% or more).
Payment Modes: The fee can be paid online through Net Banking, or Credit/Debit cards.
2. Filling Details & Uploading Documents:
Personal & Educational Information: Fill in all required details carefully, ensuring they match your official documents.

Scanned Photograph & Signature: You need to upload a recent live webcam photo and scanned copies of your signature in Hindi and English. The documents must adhere to strict specifications mentioned in the notification.
✅ Stage 3: Final Submission and Post-Submission Actions
Review and Submit: Before final submission, review the application preview carefully. Once submitted, changes are generally not possible outside the correction window.
Download Application PDF: After successful submission, download the system-generated PDF copy of your application form for your records.
Application Correction Window: BPSC may provide a brief window after the application period closes to allow candidates to make corrections.
⚠️ Common Mistakes to Avoid
Last-Minute Rush: Applying on the last day often leads to technical glitches and payment failures. Apply early.
Incorrect Photo/Signature: Uploading unclear images or documents not conforming to the specified format can lead to rejection.

Category Certificate Issues: Candidates claiming reservation must ensure their caste/residence/EWS/NCL certificates are issued by the competent authority of Bihar and are valid as per the notification.
After clearing the Prelims, candidates have to fill a separate Detailed Application Form (DAF) for the Mains exam, where they select their optional subject and provide service preferences.
Syllabus
The BPSC syllabus is the foundational document that dictates the scope of preparation. While it appears concise, each topic has a vast underlying scope.
The official notification from BPSC is the final authority on the syllabus. The following is a detailed breakdown as per the prevailing pattern.
📚 Part A: Preliminary Examination Syllabus
This paper tests a candidate's general awareness and knowledge. Questions will be of a nature that a well-educated person can answer without specialized study.
General Science (General appreciation and understanding of science, including matters of everyday observation and experience).
Current events of national and international importance.
History of India and salient features of the History of Bihar.
General Geography and Geographical division of Bihar and its major river systems.
Indian Polity and Economy and major changes in the economy of Bihar in the post-independence period.
Indian National Movement and the part played by Bihar in it.
General Mental Ability.
✒️ Part B: Main Examination Syllabus
The Mains syllabus is extensive and requires in-depth, specialized study.
The standard of this paper is of the level of Hindi taught in secondary schools of the Bihar School Examination Board. It is of a qualifying nature.
Essay (निबंध)
Grammar (व्याकरण)
Syntax (वाक्य विन्यास)
Summarization (संक्षेपण)

Modern History of India and Indian Culture: Covers the broad history of the country from the middle of the 19th century, with special focus on the history of Bihar, the introduction of Western education, the role of Bihar in the freedom struggle (including the Santhal Uprising, 1857 War of Independence, Champaran Satyagraha, Quit India Movement 1942), and features of Mauryan and Pal art and Patna Qalam painting.
Current Events of National and International Importance.

Statistical Analysis, Graphs and Diagrams: This section will include questions to test the candidate’s ability to draw conclusions from statistical, graphical or diagrammatical information and to point out deficiencies, limitations or inconsistencies therein.
Indian Polity: Questions will be based on the political system in India, including Bihar.
Indian Economy and Geography of India: Questions will test knowledge on planning in India and the physical, economic, and social geography of India, with a focus on Bihar.

The Role and Impact of Science and Technology in the Development of India: Questions will test the candidate's awareness of the role and impact of science and technology in India and Bihar, with an emphasis on applied science.

Candidates will be required to write an essay on one of several specified topics. The topics will often be related to philosophical themes, current affairs, and socio-economic issues, sometimes with a specific focus on Bihar (e.g., proverbs or 'LOKOKTI').

Candidates must choose one optional subject from a list provided by BPSC. This paper is MCQ-based and qualifying in nature . The syllabus for each optional subject is of the honours degree level. Frequently Asked Questions
Here are answers to some of the most common questions about the BPSC Civil Services Examination.
❓ Regarding Eligibility & Attempts

Can I apply for the exam while in the final year of my graduation? Yes. You are eligible to appear for the Preliminary Exam. However, you must submit proof of passing your degree when you apply for the Main Examination.

What is the cut-off date for calculating the age limit? The age limit is typically calculated as of the 1st of August of the notification year. For example, for CCE 2025, the cut-off date would be August 1, 2025.

Is there a CSAT paper in BPSC Prelims? No. The BPSC Preliminary exam consists of a single paper of General Studies. There is no separate CSAT paper.

Do the marks from the Preliminary Exam count towards the final merit list? No. The Preliminary Exam is purely a screening test. The final rank is based solely on the marks from the Main Examination (Written Merit Papers) and the Personality Test (Interview).
Is there negative marking in BPSC Prelims? Yes. As per the new pattern, there is a negative marking of one-third (1/3rd) for every incorrect answer.

What is the weightage of the Essay paper? The Essay paper holds significant weightage in the final merit list. It is for 300 marks , equal to the General Studies papers.
❓ Regarding the Interview & Final Selection

What is the DAF (Detailed Application Form)? The DAF is a comprehensive form filled by candidates who qualify for the Mains exam. It contains details about your academic, personal, and professional background. It is the primary source of information for the interview board.

How is the final rank determined? The final rank is based on the grand total of marks obtained in the Main Examination (GS-I + GS-II + Essay = 900 marks) and the Personality Test (Interview - 120 marks) , out of a total of 1020 marks.

The final merit list is prepared based on the total marks obtained in the four compulsory and optional papers of the Written Examination (excluding the qualifying papers) . The Bihar Staff Selection Commission (BSSC) Junior Engineer (JE) Examination is a state-level competitive exam conducted for the recruitment of Junior Engineers in various technical departments of the Government of Bihar. Technical Proficiency: A strong foundational knowledge in their respective engineering discipline (Civil, Mechanical, or Electrical).
Practical Application Skills: The ability to apply engineering principles to real-world problems and projects.

Syllabus
The BSSC JE syllabus is divided into two parts, corresponding to the two papers of the written exam. A thorough understanding of the syllabus is essential for focused and effective preparation.
📚 Part A: Paper I – General Studies Syllabus
This paper is common for all candidates, regardless of their engineering branch. It is divided into three sections.
Current Affairs: National and International events, major appointments, awards and honors, sports, scientific developments.
History of India & Bihar: Ancient, Medieval, and Modern History with a special focus on the Indian National Movement and the role of Bihar in it.
Geography of India & Bihar: Physical, social, and economic geography of India and Bihar, major rivers, and natural resources.
Indian Polity: Constitution of India, Panchayati Raj, Community Development, and Political System of the country.
Indian Economy: Five Year Plans, economic reforms, and key features of the Indian and Bihar economy.
General Science (Class X Level): Physics (concepts of motion, light, electricity), Chemistry (acids, bases, salts, metals, non-metals), Biology (human body, diseases, nutrition).
Mathematics (Class X Level): Number System, Percentage, Profit & Loss, Simple & Compound Interest, Average, Ratio & Proportion, Time & Work, Time & Distance.
Verbal & Non-Verbal Reasoning: Analogy, Classification, Series (Number, Alphabet), Coding-Decoding, Blood Relations, Direction Sense, Venn Diagrams, Syllogism, Problem Solving.
✒️ Part B: Paper II – Technical Syllabus
This paper covers the comprehensive syllabus of the respective engineering discipline at the diploma level.
Building Materials: Physical and Chemical properties, classification, standard tests of stones, cement, concrete, timber, paints, etc.
Surveying: Principles of surveying, chain surveying, compass traversing, leveling, theodolite traversing, tacheometry, modern surveying instruments.
Soil Mechanics: Origin of soil, phase diagram, definitions, index properties, classification of soils, permeability, compaction, shear strength.
Hydraulics: Fluid properties, hydrostatics, measurements of flow, Bernoulli’s theorem, flow through pipes, channels.
Environmental Engineering: Quality of water, sources, purification, distribution, sanitation systems, sewage treatment.

Structural Engineering (Theory of Structures, Concrete Technology, RCC & Steel Design): Bending moments and shear force diagrams, torsion, columns, basics of concrete technology, design of beams, slabs, columns, footings, and basic steel structures.
Transportation Engineering: Highway Engineering (geometric design, pavement materials, design), Railway Engineering.
Estimating, Costing and Valuation.
Basic Concepts: Concepts of resistance, inductance, capacitance, and various factors affecting them. Concepts of current, voltage, power, energy and their units.
Circuit Law: Kirchhoff’s law, Simple Circuit solution using network theorems.
AC Fundamentals: Representation of sinusoidal waveforms, peak and R.M.S. values, phasor representation, analysis of single-phase A.C. circuits.
Measurement and Measuring Instruments: Use of ammeter, voltmeter, wattmeter, megger, energy meter; AC Bridges.
Electrical Machines: D.C. Machines (construction, principles, starting and speed control), Transformers (construction, principles, regulation and efficiency), Three-phase induction motors.
Synchronous Machines: Alternators, Synchronous motors.
Generation, Transmission and Distribution: Different types of power stations, load factor, diversity factor, various types of tariffs, transmission and distribution system concepts.
Basic Electronics: Working of various electronic devices e.g. P N Junction diodes, Transistors (NPN and PNP type), BJT and JFET.
Theory of Machines and Machine Design: Simple mechanisms, Flywheels and fluctuation of energy, Power transmission by belts, clutches, and gears. Design of keys, shafts, riveted joints.
Engineering Mechanics and Strength of Materials: Laws of motion, Friction, Concept of stress and strain, Elastic limit, Bending moments and shear force diagram, Torsion of circular shafts.

Thermal Engineering: Properties of Pure Substances & Laws of Thermodynamics: P-V & P-T diagrams, First and Second Law of Thermodynamics. Air standard Cycles for IC Engines: Otto, Diesel cycles. Boilers & Rankine cycle: Principles, Classification, Specification, Fittings & Accessories.
Properties of Pure Substances & Laws of Thermodynamics: P-V & P-T diagrams, First and Second Law of Thermodynamics.
Air standard Cycles for IC Engines: Otto, Diesel cycles.
Boilers & Rankine cycle: Principles, Classification, Specification, Fittings & Accessories.
Fluid Mechanics & Machinery: Properties & Classification of fluids, Bernoulli’s equation, Measurement of flow rate, Hydraulic Turbines, Centrifugal Pumps.
Production Engineering: Classification of steels, heat treatment, welding, brazing, soldering, casting, forging, machining processes (lathe, milling, drilling, shaping).
Frequently Asked Questions
Here are answers to some common questions that BSSC JE aspirants often have.
❓ Regarding Eligibility

Can candidates with a B.E./B.Tech degree apply for the BSSC JE exam? Generally, yes. If the minimum eligibility is a Diploma in Engineering, candidates with a higher equivalent qualification like B.E./B.Tech in the same branch are usually considered eligible. However, it is crucial to read the specific eligibility clause in the official notification, as the rules can sometimes vary.

Are candidates from outside Bihar eligible for reservation benefits? No. Reservation benefits such as age relaxation and reservation of seats are applicable only to candidates who are permanent residents (domicile) of Bihar. Candidates from other states, if eligible to apply, will be considered under the Unreserved (General) category.

I am in the final year of my diploma. Can I apply? Usually no. Most BSSC notifications require the candidate to have passed the qualifying examination and possess the certificate on or before the application's closing date. Final-year or "appearing" candidates are typically not eligible unless explicitly stated in the advertisement.
❓ Regarding the Examination

Is there an interview in the selection process? No. The selection for BSSC Junior Engineer is typically based solely on the marks obtained in the written examination, followed by document verification. There is no personality test or interview.

What is the marking scheme for the exam? For each correct answer, you get +4 marks , and for each incorrect answer, there is a penalty of -1 mark . No marks are awarded or deducted for unattempted questions.
Can I use a calculator in the examination hall? No. The use of calculators, log tables, mobile phones, and any other electronic gadgets is strictly prohibited inside the examination hall.
What will be the language of the question paper? The question paper will be bilingual, i.e., printed in both Hindi and English .
❓ Regarding the Application Process

It is extremely important to review all details carefully before submitting the form. In some cases, a window for editing might be provided, but this is not guaranteed.

I forgot to take a printout of my application. What should I do? The application printout is a crucial document required during document verification. BSSC's online portal may have an option to reprint the application form by logging in with your credentials. It is advisable to download and save a PDF copy immediately after submission.

UPSC Central Armed Police Forces (Assistant Commandants) Examination
About the Examination

The Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) Central Armed Police Forces (CAPF) Examination is a national-level competitive exam for the recruitment of Assistant Commandants (AC) , who are Group 'A' officers. This examination serves as the unified gateway for aspiring candidates to join the officer cadre of India's premier internal security forces. It is a highly respected career path that offers a unique blend of adventure, responsibility, and service to the nation.
📜 The Philosophy Behind the Examination

The CAPF (AC) examination is designed to select young, dynamic, and resilient leaders. Beyond academic knowledge, the selection process rigorously assesses a candidate's physical and mental fortitude, integrity, and suitability for command roles in challenging operational environments. The exam seeks individuals who possess:
Physical and Mental Robustness: The ability to endure tough physical conditions and maintain composure under extreme pressure.
Leadership and Command Quality: The potential to lead a company of armed personnel, make critical decisions, and inspire confidence.
Intellectual Acuity: A strong grasp of general awareness, analytical reasoning, and security-related issues.
Unwavering Integrity: A strong moral compass and a deep sense of patriotism and duty.
🛡️ The Forces at Stake

Successful candidates are appointed as Assistant Commandants in one of the five Central Armed Police Forces under the Ministry of Home Affairs. These forces are the pillars of India's internal security architecture.
🪜 The Three-Stage Selection Process
The CAPF (AC) selection is a multi-stage process designed to comprehensively evaluate a candidate's fitness for the role. The entire cycle spans over a year.

Stage 1: Written Examination: This is the first filter and consists of two papers conducted on the same day. Paper I is an objective test of General Ability and Intelligence, while Paper II is a descriptive test of General Studies, Essay, and Comprehension. This stage assesses the academic and analytical capabilities of the candidates.

Stage 2: Physical Standards Test (PST) / Physical Efficiency Test (PET) & Medical Standards Test: Candidates who qualify the written exam are called for this stage. The PST involves checking physical measurements like height and chest. The PET includes a series of athletic events to test physical endurance and agility. This is followed by a detailed medical examination to ensure candidates meet the stringent health requirements. This stage is qualifying in nature .

Stage 3: Interview / Personality Test: The final stage is an interview conducted by a board of senior officers and experts at the UPSC. This test assesses the candidate's personality, leadership potential, communication skills, and overall suitability for a command position in the armed police forces.
🏆 The Final Verdict: Merit and Allocation

The final merit list is prepared based on the total marks obtained in the Written Examination (450 marks) and the Interview/Personality Test (150 marks) , for a grand total of 600 marks. Based on their final rank and the preferences submitted by them, candidates are allocated to one of the five CAPFs.
Typical Timeline (Indicative)
The UPSC CAPF (AC) Examination follows a relatively predictable annual schedule. Understanding this timeline is essential for planning your preparation effectively.
⚠️ Disclaimer: These timelines are based on past trends. Always refer to the official UPSC calendar for the specific year for exact dates.
Phase 1: Notification & Application (April - May)
Late April: The official notification for the CAPF (AC) Examination is released by UPSC on its website (upsc.gov.in).
April - May: The online application window opens and typically remains active for about 20-25 days.
Phase 2: Written Examination (August)
July: The e-Admit Card for the Written Examination is released approximately 3 weeks before the exam date.
First Sunday of August: The Written Examination (Paper I & Paper II) is conducted on a single day across the country.
Phase 3: Written Exam Result (September - October)
The results of the Written Examination are typically declared within 40-50 days. A list of qualified candidates is published, who must then fill a Detailed Application Form (DAF).
Phase 4: PST / PET & Medical Tests (December - February)
Qualified candidates are called for the Physical and Medical tests. These are conducted in batches at various centers designated by the Nodal Authority (like ITBP, BSF, etc.).
Phase 5: Interview / Personality Test (May - June of next year)
Candidates who clear the physical and medical tests are summoned for the final interview at the UPSC office in New Delhi.
Phase 6: Final Result Declaration (July - August of next year)
The final merit list, based on the combined scores of the Written Examination and Interview, is declared, marking the end of the selection cycle.
Eligibility Criteria
The eligibility criteria for the CAPF (AC) exam are very strict, especially regarding age and physical standards. Candidates must verify their eligibility meticulously.
⚠️ Note: The official UPSC notification is the ultimate authority on all eligibility criteria.
🌍 1. Nationality
A candidate must be a citizen of India . (Subjects of Nepal and Bhutan are not eligible).
🎂 2. Age Limit
The age is calculated as of the 1st of August of the examination year.
Minimum Age: 20 years .
Maximum Age: 25 years . (A candidate must not have attained the age of 25 years).
🎓 3. Educational Qualification

A candidate must hold a Bachelor's degree from a University incorporated by an Act of the Central or State Legislature in India or other educational institutions established by an Act of Parliament or declared to be deemed as a University.
🏃 4. Physical and Medical Standards
This is a critical, non-negotiable criterion. Candidates must meet the prescribed physical and medical standards.
Distant Vision (Corrected): Better Eye (6/6 or 6/9) & Worse Eye (6/12 or 6/9).
Near Vision: Better Eye (N6) & Worse Eye (N9).
Candidates must not have knock knees, flat feet, varicose veins, or squint in their eyes. They should be in good mental and bodily health.
Stages, Exam Pattern & Marking Scheme
The CAPF (AC) selection process is a comprehensive three-stage journey.
📝 Stage 1: Written Examination (Total 450 Marks)
Conducted on a single day in two sessions.
Negative Marking: There is a penalty of one-third (1/3rd) of the marks for each wrong answer in Paper I only.
Evaluation Rule: Paper II is only evaluated for those candidates who secure a minimum qualifying mark in Paper I, as decided by the commission.
🏃 Stage 2: Physical Efficiency Test (PET) - Qualifying
Candidates must qualify in all the following events. Failure in any one event leads to disqualification.
🗣️ Stage 3: Interview / Personality Test (150 Marks)

Candidates who clear the PET and are declared medically fit are called for the interview. The board assesses their suitability for a command role, evaluating their mental alertness, critical thinking, leadership qualities, and overall personality.
📊 Final Rank Calculation
The final merit list is prepared based on the marks from the Written Exam and the Interview.
Written Exam (Paper I + II): 450 Marks + Interview / Personality Test: 150 Marks = Grand Total: 600 Marks
Application Workflow
The application for the UPSC CAPF (ACs) exam is a completely online process conducted through the official UPSC website. It requires careful attention to detail to avoid rejection.
📝 Stage 1: One-Time Registration (OTR)

This is a mandatory, one-time process for all UPSC exams. Candidates must register on the OTR platform (upsconline.nic.in), providing basic details like name, date of birth, mobile number, and email ID. This information is saved and auto-populated for future applications, and it can be updated.
✍️ Stage 2: Filling the Examination Application Form
After completing OTR, candidates can log in and apply for the specific CAPF (ACs) Examination. This involves:
Part-I Registration: Confirming personal and educational details, and crucially, selecting preferences for the forces (e.g., BSF, CRPF, CISF, ITBP, SSB).

Part-II Registration: This involves paying the application fee, selecting the examination center, and uploading a recent photograph, signature, and a valid Photo ID document (like Aadhar Card, Voter ID, etc.) as per the specified format.
Amount: A non-refundable fee of ₹200 (Rupees Two Hundred only).
Exemptions: Female candidates and candidates belonging to Scheduled Caste (SC) and Scheduled Tribe (ST) categories are exempted from paying the fee.
Payment Modes: The fee can be paid online via Net Banking, UPI, or Credit/Debit cards, or offline by depositing cash at an SBI branch.
Centre Selection: Exam centers are allotted on a "first-apply-first-allot" basis for the Written Exam. Apply early to get your preferred center.
Document Specifications: Ensure your photograph, signature, and Photo ID upload meet the exact size, format, and clarity requirements mentioned in the official notification to avoid rejection.
Syllabus
The syllabus for the CAPF (AC) exam is designed to test a candidate's broad-based knowledge and analytical skills.
📚 Paper I: General Ability and Intelligence (250 Marks)
General Mental Ability: Logical Reasoning, Quantitative Aptitude (including Numerical Ability and Data Interpretation).

General Science: General awareness, scientific temper, comprehension and appreciation of scientific phenomena of everyday observation including new areas of importance like Information Technology, Biotechnology, Environmental Science.

Current Events of National and International Importance: Knowledge of current events of national and international importance in the spheres of culture, music, arts, literature, sports, governance, societal and developmental issues, industry, business, globalisation, and interplay among nations.

Indian Polity and Economy: India’s political system and the Constitution of India, social systems and public administration, economic development in India, regional and international security issues and human rights including its indicators.
History of India: Social, economic and political aspects of the History of India. Also includes the areas of growth of nationalism and freedom movement.
Indian and World Geography: Physical, social and economic aspects of geography pertaining to India and the World.
✒️ Paper II: General Studies, Essay and Comprehension (200 Marks)

Candidates have to write descriptive essays on given topics. The topics are related to modern Indian history especially of the freedom struggle, geography, polity and economy, knowledge of security and human rights issues, and analytical ability. The essays can be written in either English or Hindi .
This part consists of Comprehension passages, précis writing, developing counter arguments, report writing, and language/grammar based questions. This part must be attempted in English only .
Frequently Asked Questions
Here are answers to some common questions about the UPSC CAPF (AC) Examination.
❓ Regarding Eligibility & Application

Can I apply for the CAPF exam in the final year of my graduation? Yes. You are eligible to apply, but you must produce proof of passing your degree at the time of submitting the Detailed Application Form (DAF), which is after the written exam result.

Is there a limit on the number of attempts? No. There is no limit on the number of attempts, provided you fulfill the age criteria. You can appear for the exam as many times as you want between the ages of 20 and 25 (with relaxations for reserved categories).

Are there any relaxations in height for candidates from hilly regions? Yes. Relaxations in physical standards, including height, are available for candidates belonging to specified categories like Garhwalis, Kumaonis, Gorkhas, and those from certain North-Eastern states, as detailed in the official notification.
❓ Regarding the Examination
Is there negative marking in both papers? No. Negative marking of 1/3rd of the marks is applicable for incorrect answers in Paper I only . There is no negative marking in the descriptive Paper II.

Can I write the entire Paper II in Hindi? No. Only Part-A (Essay) of Paper II can be written in either English or Hindi. Part-B (Comprehension, Précis Writing, etc.) must be attempted in English only .

What happens if I fail the Physical Efficiency Test (PET)? Failure to qualify in any of the PET events will lead to immediate disqualification. Your candidature for that year's examination will be cancelled, and you will not proceed to the medical examination or interview stage.

UPSC Combined Defence Services Examination
About the Examination

The Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) Combined Defence Services (CDS) Examination is a prestigious national-level exam conducted twice a year to recruit Commissioned Officers into the Indian Armed Forces. Unlike civilian services, the CDS exam is the primary gateway for university graduates to embark on a challenging and honourable career leading the men and women of the Indian Army, Navy, and Air Force.
🎖️ The Philosophy Behind the Examination

The CDS selection process is designed to identify candidates who possess the unique blend of attributes required for military leadership, often summarized as "Officer Like Qualities" (OLQs). The exam assesses more than academic knowledge; it seeks individuals with:
Mental Robustness & Aptitude: The ability to think clearly, solve problems logically, and perform under pressure.
Physical Fitness & Courage: A high standard of physical and mental endurance to meet the demanding nature of military life.
Leadership & Integrity: The potential to lead, inspire confidence, and uphold the highest standards of honour and integrity.
Patriotism & Sense of Duty: A deep-seated commitment to the nation and an unwavering sense of duty and responsibility.
✈️ The Academies at Stake
Successful candidates are admitted to different defence academies based on their preference and merit. The CDS exam serves as the entry point for the following prestigious institutions:
🪜 The Two-Stage Selection Process
The CDS selection is a comprehensive two-stage process designed to thoroughly evaluate a candidate's suitability for a commission in the Armed Forces.

Stage 1: Written Examination: This is an objective-type (MCQ) examination designed to test the candidate's knowledge of English, General Knowledge, and Elementary Mathematics. It serves as a screening test to select candidates for the next stage. Candidates applying only for the Officers' Training Academy (OTA) are exempted from the Mathematics paper.

Stage 2: Services Selection Board (SSB) Interview: Candidates who qualify in the written exam are called for the SSB Interview. This is an intensive 5-day personality and intelligence assessment. It includes a battery of psychological tests, group tasks, and a personal interview to evaluate a candidate's "Officer Like Qualities" (OLQs). This stage is the ultimate test of one's character, leadership potential, and mental fortitude.
🏆 The Final Verdict: Merit and Joining Instructions

A final merit list is prepared based on the total marks obtained in the Written Examination and the SSB Interview . Candidates who clear the medical examination are issued joining instructions for their respective academies based on their rank, preferences, and the number of vacancies available.
Typical Timeline (Indicative)

The CDS Examination is conducted biannually, providing two opportunities each year for aspiring candidates. The two cycles are referred to as CDS (I) and CDS (II) . The timeline for each cycle spans approximately 9-10 months from notification to the commencement of the course.
⚠️ Disclaimer: These timelines are illustrative. Always refer to the official UPSC calendar for exact dates.
Typical Timeline for a Single CDS Cycle:
Phase 1: Notification & Application (e.g., Oct-Nov for CDS I / May-Jun for CDS II) The official notification is released by UPSC, and the online application window opens for about 20-25 days.
Phase 2: Admit Card Release (e.g., Jan-Feb for CDS I / Aug for CDS II) E-Admit cards are made available for download from the UPSC website around 3 weeks before the exam date.
Phase 3: Written Examination (e.g., Feb or Apr for CDS I / Sep for CDS II) The objective-type written exam is conducted on a single day across various centers in India.
Phase 4: Written Examination Result (e.g., Mar-May for CDS I / Oct-Nov for CDS II) UPSC declares the results of the written exam, publishing a list of qualified candidates' roll numbers.

Phase 5: SSB Interview Process (Spans Several Months) Qualified candidates are allotted dates for their 5-day SSB interviews. This phase is conducted by the respective services (Army, Navy, Air Force) and can take place over several months following the written result.
Phase 6: Final Result Declaration (e.g., Jul-Aug for CDS I / Feb-Mar for CDS II) A final merit list is published, containing the names of candidates recommended after the SSB interviews.
Phase 7: Course Commencement (e.g., Jan for CDS I / Jul for CDS II) Following medical examinations and other formalities, the course commences at the respective training academies.
Eligibility Criteria
Eligibility for the CDS Examination is highly specific and varies for each academy. Key criteria include nationality, age, marital status, and educational qualifications.
⚠️ Note: The official UPSC notification for the specific examination cycle is the final authority on all eligibility conditions.
🌍 1. Nationality
A candidate must be unmarried and must either be:
a Citizen of India, or
a subject of Nepal, or

a person of Indian origin who has migrated from Pakistan, Burma, Sri Lanka and East African Countries of Kenya, Uganda, the United Republic of Tanzania, Zambia, Malawi, Zaire and Ethiopia or Vietnam with the intention of permanently settling in India.
💍 2. Marital Status
For IMA, INA, and AFA: Candidates must be unmarried males .
For OTA (Men & Women): Candidates (both male and female) must be unmarried .
Candidates must not marry during the period of training. Marriage during training will result in discharge from the academy.
🎂 3. Age Limit & Educational Qualification
Age and educational requirements are distinct for each academy and are strictly enforced.

Note for Final-Year Students: Candidates who are in their final year/semester of a degree course are also eligible to apply, provided they can produce proof of passing the degree examination by the specified date mentioned in the official notification.
Stages & Exam Pattern
The CDS selection process is a two-stage affair: a written exam followed by an SSB interview for qualified candidates.
🎯 Stage 1: Written Examination (Objective Type)
The pattern of the written exam differs for candidates aspiring for IMA, INA, and AFA versus those for the OTA.
Objective Format: All papers consist of Multiple Choice Questions (MCQs).
Negative Marking: There is a penalty for wrong answers. One-third (0.33) of the marks assigned to a question will be deducted for each incorrect answer.
Language of Paper: The question papers for General Knowledge and Elementary Mathematics will be set bilingually in Hindi as well as English.
🗣️ Stage 2: Services Selection Board (SSB) Interview

This is a comprehensive personality and intelligence test conducted over 5 days. It is not an academic knowledge test but an evaluation of "Officer Like Qualities" (OLQs). The SSB process is divided into two stages.

Stage I (Screening): This is a one-day screening process involving an Officer Intelligence Rating (OIR) test and a Picture Perception & Description Test (PPDT). Candidates who clear Stage I proceed to Stage II.
Psychological Tests: Thematic Apperception Test (TAT), Word Association Test (WAT), Situation Reaction Test (SRT), and Self Description Test (SD).
Group Testing Officer (GTO) Tasks: A series of indoor and outdoor group exercises, including group discussions, group planning exercises, and command tasks.
Personal Interview: A one-on-one conversation with a senior officer (the Interviewing Officer).
Conference: On the final day, all assessors jointly discuss each candidate's performance before finalizing their recommendation.
📊 Final Merit Calculation
The final merit list is prepared based on the combined marks of the Written Exam and the SSB Interview.
For IMA, INA, AFA: Written Exam (300) + SSB Interview (300) = Total 600 Marks For OTA: Written Exam (200) + SSB Interview (200) = Total 400 Marks
Application Workflow
The application for the UPSC CDS exam is a completely online process conducted through the official UPSC website. It requires careful attention to detail to avoid rejection.
📝 Stage 1: One-Time Registration (OTR)

This is a mandatory, one-time process for all UPSC exams. Candidates must register on the OTR platform, providing basic details like name, date of birth, mobile number, and email ID. This information is saved and auto-populated for future applications.
✍️ Stage 2: Filling the Examination Application Form
After OTR, candidates can log in and apply for the specific CDS Examination. This involves:
Part-I Registration: Confirming personal and educational details, and crucially, selecting preferences for the academies (IMA, INA, AFA, OTA).
Part-II Registration: This involves paying the application fee, selecting the examination center, and uploading a recent photograph and signature as per the specified format.
Amount: A non-refundable fee of ₹200 (Rupees Two Hundred only).
Exemptions: Female candidates and candidates belonging to Scheduled Caste (SC) and Scheduled Tribe (ST) categories are exempted from paying the fee.
Payment Modes: The fee can be paid online via Net Banking, UPI, or Credit/Debit cards, or offline via cash deposit at an SBI branch.
Centre Selection: Exam centers are allotted on a "first-apply-first-allot" basis. Apply early to get your preferred center.
Document Specifications: Ensure your photograph and signature uploads meet the exact size and format requirements mentioned in the notification.
Syllabus

The standard of the papers in Elementary Mathematics will be of Matriculation level. The standard of papers in other subjects will approximately be such as may be expected of a graduate of an Indian University.
Paper I: English (100 Marks)

DRDO Scientist Entry Test
About the Examination

The Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) is the premier R&D wing of the Ministry of Defence, Govt. of India, with a vision to empower India with cutting-edge defence technologies. The Scientist Entry Test (SET) is a highly competitive recruitment process conducted by DRDO's Recruitment & Assessment Centre (RAC) to induct the nation's brightest engineering and science graduates as Scientist 'B' , a Group 'A' Gazetted technical service of the Union.
🔬 The Philosophy Behind the Recruitment

Unlike conventional exams, the DRDO selection process is designed to identify individuals with a strong aptitude for research, development, and innovation. The core philosophy is to assess a candidate's:
Fundamental Knowledge: A deep and clear understanding of core engineering principles.
Practical Application: The ability to apply theoretical knowledge to solve real-world, complex problems in defence technology.
Research Aptitude: A curious and analytical mind with the potential to contribute to novel research and development projects.
Commitment to National Security: A dedication to serving the nation by contributing to its technological self-reliance in defence.
🚀 The Role of a Scientist 'B'

A career as a DRDO Scientist is one of the most prestigious technical jobs in the country. New recruits are involved in the design, development, testing, and evaluation of state-of-the-art systems across a wide spectrum of technologies, including:
🪜 The Two-Stage Selection Process
The selection is a rigorous two-stage process designed to filter for exceptional technical talent.

Stage 1: Shortlisting (The Technical Screen): This is the initial filtering stage. For most engineering disciplines, candidates are shortlisted based on their valid GATE (Graduate Aptitude Test in Engineering) scores . For some specific roles, a separate descriptive written examination may be conducted. The goal is to identify a pool of candidates with proven proficiency in their engineering domain.

Stage 2: Personal Interview (The Final Assessment): Shortlisted candidates are called for a final, in-depth personal interview. This is a crucial stage conducted by a panel of senior DRDO scientists and subject matter experts. It aims to assess the candidate's technical knowledge, practical understanding, problem-solving skills, and suitability for a research and development environment.
🏆 The Final Verdict: Merit and Appointment

The final merit list is prepared based on a weighted score combining the performance in GATE and the Personal Interview , or the Written Exam and the Interview. Successful candidates receive an offer of appointment as Scientist 'B' and undergo an induction program before being posted to one of DRDO's many laboratories or establishments across India.
Typical Timeline (Indicative)

Unlike the fixed calendar of UPSC, the DRDO recruitment timeline is dynamic and depends on the vacancies advertised. The entire process, from notification to the final result, typically spans 6-8 months.
⚠️ Disclaimer: This timeline is indicative. Always refer to the official RAC website for the exact schedule of a specific recruitment advertisement.
Phase 1: Notification & Application (Variable)
DRDO releases advertisements on the RAC website (rac.gov.in) and in the Employment News as per requirement. There is no fixed annual schedule.
The online application window typically remains open for 21-30 days from the date of notification.
Phase 2: Scrutiny and Shortlisting (1-2 Months Post Application)

Candidates are shortlisted for the next stage (Interview or Written Exam) based on their GATE scores or other criteria mentioned in the advertisement.

If a written exam is part of the selection process for a particular discipline, it is conducted after the initial shortlisting. Admit cards are released about 2-3 weeks before the exam date.
Phase 4: Personal Interviews (2-4 Months Post Application)
Interview call letters are issued to shortlisted candidates via email and the RAC portal.
Interviews are typically conducted in person at the DRDO headquarters in Delhi or other designated centers. The interview schedule is spread over several weeks.
Phase 5: Final Result Declaration (1-2 Months Post Interview)
The final merit list, based on the combined weighted scores, is published on the RAC website.

GATE Qualification: A valid GATE (Graduate Aptitude Test in Engineering) score in the specified GATE paper is mandatory for most engineering disciplines. The advertisement will specify the eligible GATE papers (e.g., EC for Electronics, ME for Mechanical, CS for Computer Science).

The DRDO selection process is designed to evaluate deep technical knowledge and research potential. It is primarily based on GATE scores and a Personal Interview.
🎯 Stage 1: Shortlisting based on GATE Score
This is the first and most critical filter.
Basis: Candidates are shortlisted for the interview based on their valid GATE scores in the relevant paper.
Ratio: The shortlisting is done in a ratio of approximately 1:10 (10 candidates for every 1 vacancy) for each discipline and category.

Cut-off: RAC releases the category-wise GATE score cut-offs for shortlisting after the process is complete. These cut-offs vary significantly each year based on the number of vacancies and the performance of applicants.

Purpose: To test the in-depth theoretical knowledge and problem-solving ability of the candidates.

❓ Regarding Eligibility & GATE Score

Can I apply while in my final year of B.E./B.Tech? Yes. Final year students are generally eligible to apply. However, you must have completed your degree and be able to produce the provisional/final certificate by a specified date mentioned in the advertisement, which is usually before the interviews.

Is a GATE score compulsory to apply? For almost all Scientist 'B' posts in engineering disciplines, a valid GATE score is mandatory . It is the primary criterion for shortlisting. Which year's GATE score is considered valid? The advertisement will clearly specify this. Usually, the GATE score of the current year is valid. Sometimes, DRDO also allows scores from the previous one or two years. For example, a 2025 advertisement might accept GATE 2023, 2024, and 2025 scores.
