UPSC Engineering Services Examination
About the Examination
📜 The Philosophy Behind the Examination

The ESE is engineered to assess more than just theoretical knowledge. Its core philosophy is to identify individuals who possess a potent combination of deep technical expertise, robust analytical and problem-solving skills, and strong leadership potential . The examination seeks to evaluate a candidate's:
Technical Competence: A thorough and profound understanding of the fundamental principles of their engineering discipline.
Problem-Solving Ability: The capacity to apply engineering concepts to solve complex, real-world problems efficiently and innovatively.
Managerial Acumen: The potential to lead teams, manage large-scale projects, and make sound technical and administrative decisions under pressure.
Ethical Foundation: A strong sense of professional ethics, integrity, and a commitment to public service and national development.
Aptitude and General Awareness: A broad awareness of current affairs, general studies, and logical reasoning, which are essential for a well-rounded technocrat.
🏛️ The Services and Disciplines

The ESE is conducted for recruitment into four main engineering disciplines. Successful candidates are allocated to various Group 'A' and Group 'B' services based on their rank, preferences, and the vacancies in their respective disciplines.
The four engineering disciplines are:
Some of the key services under these categories include:
and many others across various ministries and departments.
🪜 The Three-Tiered Selection Gauntlet

The ESE is a multi-layered process where each stage is designed to filter candidates based on specific skills and knowledge. The entire cycle, from notification to the final result, spans over a year.

Stage 1: Preliminary Examination (The Technical Screen): This is an objective-type (Multiple Choice Questions) screening test comprising two papers. Paper-I tests General Studies and Engineering Aptitude, while Paper-II is discipline-specific. Its primary role is to select candidates with a solid foundation in both general and technical areas for the next stage. Crucially, the marks from this stage are not counted for the final merit list.

Stage 3: Personality Test (The Professional Appraisal): The final stage is an interview conducted by a board of experts at the UPSC headquarters in New Delhi. This interview assesses the candidate's suitability for a career in public service from a technical and managerial perspective. The board evaluates leadership qualities, initiative, intellectual curiosity, mental and physical energy, and other traits required for a successful career as an engineer in a government service.
🏆 The Final Verdict: Merit and Allocation

The final merit list is prepared based on the total marks obtained in the Main Examination (600 marks) and the Personality Test (200 marks) , for a grand total of 800 marks. Based on their final rank in their specific engineering discipline, the preferences for services submitted by them, their category, and the vacancies available, candidates are recommended for appointment to various engineering services under the Government of India.
Typical Timeline (Indicative)

The UPSC Engineering Services Examination is a marathon that unfolds over a period of 12-14 months, from the date of notification to the declaration of the final result. Understanding this timeline is crucial for strategic planning and sustained preparation. The following is a typical, indicative schedule based on past trends.
⚠️ Disclaimer: These timelines are based on past trends. Always refer to the official UPSC calendar for the specific year for exact dates.
Phase 1: Notification & Application (September - October)

Mid to Late September: The official notification for the Engineering Services Examination is released by UPSC on its website (upsc.gov.in). This document contains all essential details: vacancy numbers, eligibility criteria, syllabus, exam rules, and the list of examination centers.

September - October: The online application window opens on the day of the notification and typically remains active for about 20-25 days . This process involves a one-time registration (OTR) and filling out the application form. Aspirants must be extremely careful while filling in their engineering discipline, selecting centers, and uploading documents.
Phase 2: Prelims Preparation & Admit Card (January - February)
November - January: This is a period of intense, focused preparation and revision for the Preliminary Examination.
Late January / Early February: Approximately 3 weeks before the exam date , UPSC releases the e-Admit Card for the Preliminary Examination. Candidates must download and print it.
Phase 3: Preliminary Examination (February)

The Preliminary Exam is conducted on a single day (usually a Sunday in February). It consists of two compulsory papers with a break in between. Paper I: General Studies & Engineering Aptitude (10:00 AM to 12:00 PM) Paper II: Engineering Discipline Specific (2:00 PM to 5:00 PM)
Paper I: General Studies & Engineering Aptitude (10:00 AM to 12:00 PM)
Paper II: Engineering Discipline Specific (2:00 PM to 5:00 PM)
Phase 4: Mains Qualification & DAF-I (April - May)
Late March / Early April: The results of the Preliminary Examination are typically declared within 30-40 days of the exam date. UPSC releases a list of the roll numbers of qualified candidates.

April - May: Shortly after the Prelims result, the qualified candidates are required to fill out the Detailed Application Form-I (DAF-I) . This is an exhaustive form that collects detailed information about the candidate's personal background, educational qualifications, and service preferences. This form is the basis for the interview later on.
Phase 5: Main Examination (June / July)
May / June: Admit cards for the Main Examination are released for candidates who have successfully submitted their DAF-I.

June / July: The Main Examination is a descriptive (written) test conducted on a single day, with two sessions for the two discipline-specific papers. It tests the depth of a candidate's technical knowledge and problem-solving ability.
Phase 6: Personality Test Qualification (September / October)

September / October: The results of the Main Examination are usually announced about 2 to 3 months after the exam. A list of candidates who have qualified for the Personality Test (Interview) is published.
Phase 7: Personality Tests (Interviews) (October - December)
The Personality Tests (Interviews) typically commence a few weeks after the Mains results are declared.
Candidates are summoned to the UPSC office (Dholpur House) in New Delhi in batches. The interview schedule is spread over several weeks.
Phase 8: Final Result Declaration (December / January)

This is the culmination of the entire process. The final merit list, based on the combined scores of the Main Examination and the Personality Test, is declared. This usually happens within 10-15 days of the conclusion of the last interview.
Eligibility Criteria

Before embarking on the rigorous journey of UPSC ESE preparation, every aspirant must meticulously verify their eligibility. The criteria set by the Union Public Service Commission are strict and non-negotiable. Eligibility is primarily determined by three key parameters: Nationality, Age Limit, and Educational Qualification.
⚠️ Note: The details provided here are based on prevailing rules. These are subject to change, and the official UPSC notification for the current examination year is the ultimate authority.
🌍 1. Nationality
A candidate for the Engineering Services Examination must be one of the following:
A citizen of India, or
A subject of Nepal, or
A subject of Bhutan, or
A Tibetan refugee who came over to India before the 1st of January, 1962, with the intention of permanently settling in India, or

A person of Indian origin (PIO) who has migrated from Pakistan, Burma, Sri Lanka, East African countries of Kenya, Uganda, the United Republic of Tanzania, Zambia, Malawi, Zaire, Ethiopia and Vietnam with the intention of permanently settling in India.
Candidates belonging to the latter categories must possess a certificate of eligibility issued by the Government of India.
🎂 2. Age Limit
The age of a candidate is calculated as of a specific cut-off date, which is typically the 1st of January of the examination year. The general age limits are as follows:
Minimum Age: A candidate must have attained the age of 21 years .
Maximum Age: A candidate must not have attained the age of 30 years (for the General category).
This means a candidate from the General category must have been born not earlier than 2nd January, 1996 and not later than 1st January, 2005 (for the 2026 exam, as an example).

🎓 3. Educational Qualification
This is the most critical eligibility criterion for ESE. The minimum educational requirement is:

A candidate must have obtained an Engineering Degree from a University incorporated by an Act of the Central or State Legislature in India or other Educational Institutions established by an Act of Parliament or declared to be deemed as Universities under Section 3 of the University Grants Commission Act, 1956.
Alternatively, a candidate must have passed Sections A and B of the Institution Examinations of the Institution of Engineers (India).
Obtained a degree/diploma in Engineering from such foreign University/College/Institution and under such conditions as may be recognised by the Government for the purpose from time to time.
Passed Graduate Membership Examination of the Institution of Electronics and Telecommunication Engineers (India).
Passed Associate Membership Examination Parts II and III/Sections A and B of the Aeronautical Society of India.

Final-Year Students: Candidates who have appeared or intend to appear for their final degree examination and are awaiting results are also eligible to apply. However, they must produce proof of passing the said examination along with the Detailed Application Form (DAF-I) for the Main Examination.
The degree must be in one of the four eligible disciplines: Civil, Mechanical, Electrical, or Electronics & Telecommunication Engineering .
✍️ 4. Number of Attempts

There is no restriction on the number of times a candidate can appear for the ESE. Candidates can attempt the examination as many times as they wish, provided they fulfill the age limit and other eligibility criteria specified in the examination notification.
Stages, Exam Pattern & Marking Scheme

The Engineering Services Examination is a meticulously designed three-stage process. Each stage has a distinct purpose, format, and evaluation methodology. A thorough understanding of this pattern is the first step toward building a successful preparation strategy.
🎯 Stage 1: Preliminary Examination (Objective Type)

The primary purpose of the Prelims is to screen candidates for the Main Examination. It tests both general aptitude and core engineering knowledge. The marks obtained in this stage are not counted for the final merit list.
Objective Format: Both papers consist of Multiple Choice Questions (MCQs).
Negative Marking: There is a penalty for incorrect answers. For each wrong answer, one-third (1/3rd) of the marks assigned to that question will be deducted.

Cut-off Calculation: The cut-off for qualifying for the Main Examination is determined based on the total marks scored in both Paper I and Paper II. There are minimum qualifying marks for each paper as decided by the commission.
📝 Stage 2: Main Examination (Descriptive Type)

This stage is the core of the selection process and is designed to assess the in-depth technical knowledge and problem-solving skills of a candidate. The marks obtained here are the primary determinant of a candidate's final rank. It consists of 2 descriptive papers specific to the candidate's engineering stream.
Both papers are subjective and require detailed, written answers. The use of non-programmable scientific calculators is permitted in this stage.
🗣️ Stage 3: Personality Test (Interview)

The final stage is a face-to-face interview with the UPSC board. It is not just a test of technical knowledge but an assessment of the candidate's overall personality, leadership potential, and suitability for a high-responsibility technical career in the government.
Maximum Marks: 200 Marks
Basis of Interview: The conversation is largely guided by the candidate's Detailed Application Form (DAF), covering their academic and project background, work experience, and interests.
Qualities Assessed: The board evaluates leadership, initiative, intellectual curiosity, judgement, mental alertness, and the ability to apply technical knowledge to practical situations.
📊 Final Rank Calculation
The final merit list is prepared based on the cumulative score of the Main Examination and the Personality Test.
Main Exam (Written) Marks: 600 + Personality Test (Interview) Marks: 200 = Grand Total: 800 Marks
Application Workflow

The application process for the UPSC ESE is conducted exclusively online through the official UPSC website. It is a meticulous process that requires careful attention to detail. Any error can lead to the rejection of the application. The process can be broken down into several key stages.
📝 Stage 1: One-Time Registration (OTR)
Before filling out the application form for any UPSC examination, a candidate must complete the One-Time Registration. As the name suggests, this is a one-time activity.

Purpose: The OTR platform saves a candidate's basic personal information, which can then be automatically populated whenever they apply for a UPSC exam. This saves time and reduces the chance of errors in subsequent applications.

Information Required: You will need to provide your name, parents' names, date of birth, gender, minority status, a valid mobile number, a valid email ID, and details of your Class 10 board examination roll number.

Verification: The mobile number and email ID are verified through OTPs. It is crucial to use an active and personal mobile number and email, as all future communication from UPSC will be sent to them.
Permanence: The information submitted in the OTR profile is stored securely and can be updated, with some limitations, at any time.
✍️ Stage 2: Filling the Examination Application Form
Once your OTR is complete, you can log in and apply for the Engineering Services (Preliminary) Examination. This is typically a two-part process.
This part involves filling in your essential details:
Personal Information: Most of this will be auto-filled from your OTR profile. You will need to confirm details and add information like your marital status and community (General, EWS, OBC, SC, ST).
Educational Qualification: You must provide details of your engineering degree and select your engineering discipline for the exam.
Address and Contact Details: Confirmation of your mailing address.
This part involves completing the final steps of the application:
1. Fee Payment:
Amount: A non-refundable application fee of ₹200 (Rupees Two Hundred only).
Exemptions: Female candidates and candidates belonging to Scheduled Caste (SC), Scheduled Tribe (ST), and Persons with Benchmark Disability (PwBD) categories are exempted from paying the fee.

Payment Modes: The fee can be paid through: Online: Net Banking, UPI, or by using Visa/Mastercard/RuPay Credit/Debit cards. Offline: "Pay-by-Cash" mode by generating a challan and depositing the cash at any branch of the State Bank of India (SBI).

2. Uploading of Photograph, Signature, and Photo ID Card:
This is a critical step where most errors occur. The documents must adhere to strict specifications.

Scanned Photograph: Must be a recent passport-style colour picture against a white or light-coloured background. The face should cover 3/4th of the photo's space. Format: JPG/JPEG . Size: 20 KB to 300 KB .

The capacity of popular centers fills up very quickly. It is highly advisable to complete your application as early as possible to secure your preferred city.
✅ Stage 3: Final Submission and Post-Submission Actions

Review and Submit: Before final submission, the portal provides a complete preview of your application. You must review every single detail for accuracy. Once submitted, changes are generally not possible outside the correction window.
Download Application PDF: After successful submission, download the system-generated PDF copy of your application form. It is essential to keep a soft and hard copy for your records.

Application Correction Window: UPSC usually provides a brief window (typically 7 days) after the application period closes to allow candidates to make corrections to their submitted forms. However, certain core fields like the choice of examination center might not be editable.
⚠️ Common Mistakes to Avoid
Last-Minute Rush: Applying on the last day often leads to technical glitches, payment failures, and mistakes. Apply early.
Incorrect Photo/Signature: Uploading selfies, blurred images, or documents not conforming to the specified size and format can lead to application rejection.
Wrong Engineering Discipline: Double-check that you have selected the correct engineering stream (Civil, Mechanical, etc.) as this cannot be changed later.
OBC Certificate Issues: OBC candidates must ensure their Non-Creamy Layer (NCL) certificate is recent and valid for the specified financial year as per the notification.
Forgetting Final Submission: Completing Part-I but failing to complete Part-II (fee/uploads) means your application is incomplete and will be rejected.
Syllabus

The UPSC ESE syllabus is the foundational document that dictates the scope of a candidate's preparation. It is highly technical and comprehensive, designed to test a candidate's grasp of core engineering principles and their application. The syllabus is divided into a common paper for the Preliminary stage and discipline-specific papers for both Preliminary and Main stages.
The official notification from UPSC is the final authority on the syllabus. The detailed breakdown below is based on the prevailing pattern.
📚 Preliminary Stage - Paper I Syllabus
Current issues of national and international importance relating to social, economic, and industrial development.
Engineering Aptitude covering Logical reasoning and Analytical ability.
Engineering Mathematics and Numerical Analysis.
General Principles of Design, Drawing, Importance of Safety.
Standards and Quality practices in production, construction, maintenance, and services.
Basics of Energy and Environment: Conservation, environmental pollution and degradation, Climate Change, Environmental impact assessment.
Basics of Project Management.
Basics of Material Science and Engineering.
Information and Communication Technologies (ICT) based tools and their applications in engineering such as networking, e-governance, and technology-based education.
Ethics and values in the engineering profession.
✒️ Discipline-Specific Syllabus (For Prelims Paper-II & Mains Paper-I, II)
The syllabus for the Preliminary Stage (Paper-II) is derived from the comprehensive syllabus provided below for the Main Stage (Papers I & II).

Building Materials: Stone, Lime, Glass, Plastics, Steel, FRP, Ceramics, Aluminum, Fly Ash, Basic Admixtures, Timber, Bricks and Aggregates: classification, properties and selection criteria; Cement: Types, Composition, Properties, Uses, Specifications and various Tests; Lime & Mortar; Concrete: Importance of W/C Ratio, Strength, ingredients, workability, testing, mix design, storage, batching, mixing, placement, compaction, finishing and curing of concrete; repair of concrete structures.

Solid Mechanics: Elastic constants, stress, plane stress, Mohr’s circle of stress, strains, plane strain, Mohr’s circle of strain, combined stress; Elastic theories of failure; Simple bending, shear; Torsion of circular and rectangular sections and simple members.

Structural Analysis: Analysis of determinate structures - different methods; Analysis of indeterminate skeletal frames - moment distribution, slope deflection, stiffness and force methods, energy methods, Muller-Breslau principle and application; plastic analysis of beams and frames.
Design of Steel Structures: Principles of working stress methods, design of connections, simple members, Built-up sections and frames, Design of Industrial roofs; Principles of ultimate load design.

Design of Concrete and Masonry Structures: Limit state design for bending, shear, axial compression and combined forces; Design of beams, Slabs, Lintels, Foundations, Retaining walls, Tanks, Staircases; Principles of pre-stressed concrete design including materials and methods; Earthquake resistant design of structures; Design of masonry walls.

Construction Practice, Planning and Management: Construction - Planning, Equipment, Site investigation and Management including estimation with latest project management tools and network analysis for different Types of works; Analysis of Rates of various types of works; Tendering process and contract management, Quality control, Productivity, Operation cost; Land acquisition; Labour safety and welfare.

Hydrology and Water Resources Engineering: Hydrological cycle, precipitation, evaporation, transpiration, infiltration, overland flow, hydrograph, flood frequency analysis, flood routing, reservoir capacity, reservoir and channel routing, surface run-off models, ground water hydrology, steady state well hydraulics and aquifers; Application of Darcy’s law.

Environmental Engineering: Water supply engineering, water demand, sources, hydrology, ground water pumping; Water quality standards, treatment systems, distribution networks; Sewage systems, quantity, quality, treatment, disposal, reuse; Air pollution, noise pollution, and ecology.

Geo-technical Engineering and Foundation Engineering: Soil exploration, classification, properties, moisture content, voids, permeability, seepage, consolidation, shear strength; Earth pressure theories, stability of slopes, soil stabilization, foundations, bearing capacity, settlement analysis, shallow and deep foundations.

Surveying and Geology: Classification of surveys, scales, accuracy; Measurement of distance and directions; Leveling, contouring, traversing, permanent adjustments of instruments; Tachometry, trigonometric leveling; Photogrammetry, GIS, GPS; Basic Geology.

Transportation Engineering: Highways - Planning & construction, materials, pavement design, traffic engineering; Railways - Systems, alignment, components, structures, traffic; Harbours and Airports - Layouts, planning, components.

Fluid Mechanics: Basic Concepts and Properties of Fluids, Manometry, Fluid Statics, Buoyancy, Equations of Motion, Bernoulli’s equation and applications, Viscous flow of incompressible fluids, Laminar and Turbulent flows, Flow through pipes and head losses in pipes.

IC Engines, Refrigeration and Air conditioning: CI and SI Engines, two-stroke and four-stroke engines, engine components, performance characteristics, turbocharging, engine emissions and control. Vapour compression refrigeration, Refrigerants and Working cycles, Compressors, Condensers, Evaporators and Expansion devices, other types of refrigeration systems. Psychometric properties, psychometric charts, psychometric processes, cooling load calculations, ventilation and infiltration.

Turbo Machinery: Reciprocating and Rotary pumps, Pelton wheel, Kaplan and Francis Turbines, velocity diagrams, Impulse and Reaction principles, Steam and Gas Turbines, Theory of Jet Propulsion – Pulse jet and Ram Jet Engines, Reciprocating and Rotary Compressors – Theory and Applications.

Power Plant Engineering: Rankine and Brayton cycles with regeneration and reheat, Fuels and their properties, Flue gas analysis, Boilers, steam turbines and other power plant components, Steam nozzles, Nuclear power plants, Hydro-electric power plants.
Renewable Sources of Energy: Solar Radiation, Solar Thermal Energy collection and storage, Solar Photovoltaic Conversion, Wind, Geothermal and Tidal energy, Bio-mass and biofuels.

Engineering Mechanics: Analysis of force systems, Friction, Centroids and Moments of Inertia, Kinematics and dynamics of particles and rigid bodies, impulse and momentum, work-energy principles, vibrations.

Engineering Materials: Basic concepts on structure of solids, crystalline materials, defects in crystalline materials, significance of grain and grain boundaries, phase diagrams, heat treatment of steel, plastics, ceramics and composite materials.

Mechanisms and Machines: Types of Kinematics Pair, Mobility, Inversions, Kinematic Analysis, Velocity and Acceleration Analysis of Planar Mechanisms, CAMs with uniform acceleration and retardation, cycloidal motion, oscillating followers; Vibrations, Gears, Governors, Balancing of Reciprocating and Rotating masses, Gyroscopes.

Design of Machine Elements: Design for static and dynamic loading; failure theories; fatigue strength and the S-N diagram; principles of the design of machine elements such as riveted, welded and bolted joints, shafts, spur gears, rolling and sliding contact bearings, brakes and clutches, springs.

Manufacturing, Industrial and Maintenance Engineering: Metal casting, forming, joining, machining and machine-tool operations, non-conventional machining, CMM, jigs and fixtures, metrology, inspection, computer integrated manufacturing, FMS, production planning and control, inventory control, operations research, PERT and CPM, TPM, reliability, failure analysis.

Mechatronics and Robotics: Microprocessors and microcontrollers, logic gates, sensors and actuators, pneumatic and hydraulic systems, PLC, robotics, robot classification, robot specification, notations, direct and inverse kinematics.

Engineering Mathematics: Matrix theory, Eigen values & Eigen vectors, system of linear equations, Numerical methods for solution of non-linear algebraic equations and differential equations, integral calculus, partial derivatives, maxima and minima, Line, Surface and Volume Integrals, Fourier series, solution of partial differential equations, complex variables, probability and statistics.
Electrical Materials: Engineering materials, Crystal structure & defects, Ceramic materials, Insulating materials, Magnetic materials, Superconductors. Nanomaterials and their applications.

Electrical and Electronic Measurements: Principles of measurement, accuracy, precision and standards; Bridges and potentiometers, moving coil, moving iron, dynamometer and induction type instruments, measurement of voltage, current, power, energy and power factor, instrument transformers, digital voltmeters and multi-meters, phase, time and frequency measurement, Q-meters, oscilloscopes, Transducers.

Computer Fundamentals: Number systems, Boolean algebra, arithmetic functions, Basic Architecture, Central Processing Unit, I/O and Memory Organisation; peripheral devices, data representation and programming, basics of C language.

Basic Electronics Engineering: Basics of Semiconductor diodes and transistors and characteristics, Junction and field effect transistors (BJT, FET and MOSFETS), different types of transistor amplifiers, equivalent circuits and frequency response; oscillators and other circuit applications, feedback amplifiers.

Analog and Digital Electronics: Operational amplifiers, combinational and sequential logic circuits, multiplexers, multi-vibrators, sample and hold circuits, A/D and D/A converters, basics of filter circuits and applications, simple active filters.

Systems and Signal Processing: Representation of continuous and discrete-time signals, shifting and scaling operations, linear, time-invariant and causal systems, Fourier series representation of continuous periodic signals, sampling theorem, Z-transform, DFT, FFT, linear convolution, digital filter design (FIR and IIR).

Control Systems: Principles of feedback, transfer function, block diagrams and signal flow graphs, steady-state errors, Routh-Hurwitz criterion, Nyquist techniques, Bode plots, root loci, lag, lead and lead-lag compensation, state space model, state transition matrix, controllability and observability.

Electrical Machines: Single phase transformers, three phase transformers, autotransformers, DC machines, Three phase induction motors, Synchronous machines, Special machines (stepper, brushless, servo).

Power Systems: Basic power generation concepts, steam, gas and water turbines, transmission line models and performance, cable performance, insulation, corona and radio interference, power factor correction, symmetrical components, fault analysis, principles of protection systems, basics of solid state relays and digital protection; Circuit breakers, load flow studies, voltage control, power system stability.

Power Electronics and Drives: Semiconductor power diodes, transistors, thyristors, triacs, GTOs, MOSFETs and IGBTs, static characteristics and principles of operation, triggering circuits, phase control rectifiers, bridge converters, choppers and inverters, basic concepts of adjustable speed DC and AC drives, DC-DC switched mode converters, DC-AC switched mode converters.

Basic Electronics Engineering: Basics of semiconductors; Diode/Transistor basics and characteristics; Diodes for different uses; Junction & Field Effect Transistors (BJTs, JFETs, MOSFETs); Transistor amplifiers of different types, oscillators and other circuits; Basics of Integrated Circuits (ICs); Bipolar, MOS and CMOS ICs.
Basic Electrical Engineering: DC circuits, AC circuits, Single-phase and three-phase power measurement, Transformers, DC and AC machines, Power systems fundamentals.
Materials Science: Electrical Engineering materials; Crystal structures and defects; Ceramic, Insulating, Magnetic materials; Superconductivity, Nanomaterials, and their applications.

Electronic Measurements and Instrumentation: Principles of measurement, accuracy, precision, standards; Analog and Digital systems for measurement, Cathode Ray Oscilloscope, signal generators, sensitive voltmeters, data acquisition systems, instrumentation transducers.
Network Theory: Network graphs & matrices, Wye-Delta transformation, transient and steady-state analysis, frequency domain analysis, two-port networks, network synthesis.

Analog and Digital Circuits: Diode circuits, Amplifiers (BJT, FET), frequency response, Op-Amp circuits, active filters, sinusoidal oscillators; Combinational and sequential logic circuits, multiplexers, demultiplexers, Schmitt triggers, A/D and D/A converters, basics of memories.

Analog and Digital Communication Systems: Random signals and noise, AM, FM, transmitters/receivers, pulse-code modulation (PCM), differential PCM (DPCM), delta modulation (DM), digital modulation schemes (ASK, PSK, FSK), error control coding, information theory, TDMA, FDMA, CDMA, fibre optics.

Control Systems: Signal flow graphs, transient and steady-state analysis of LTI systems, Routh-Hurwitz and Nyquist criteria, Bode and root-locus plots, lead-lag compensation, PID and industrial controllers, state-space analysis, controllability and observability.

Computer Organization and Architecture: Basic architecture, CPU, I/O and memory organization, instruction sets, data representation, programming, memory management, pipelines, parallel processing basics.
Electro Magnetics: Maxwell’s equations, wave propagation in bounded and unbounded media, transmission lines, waveguides, antennas, basics of radar, optical fibre communication.
Advanced Electronics Topics: VLSI technology, VLSI design, IC fabrication, Chi-processing, photolithography, epitaxy, etching, CMOS basics, micro-fabrication, MEMS.
Advanced Communication Topics: Satellite communication, Mobile communication, Cellular concepts, GSM, CDMA, advanced mobile standards, wireless LANs, optical networking, basics of data networks.
Frequently Asked Questions
Here are answers to some of the most common questions that aspirants have about the UPSC Engineering Services Examination.
❓ Regarding Eligibility & Attempts

Can I apply for the exam while in the final year of my B.E./B.Tech? Yes. You are eligible to appear for the Preliminary Exam if you are in your final year. However, you must submit proof of passing your degree when you apply for the Main Examination (i.e., by filling the DAF-I), failing which you will be disqualified.

I have a degree in Computer Science Engineering. Am I eligible? No. As per the current rules, only candidates with a degree in one of the four specified streams— Civil, Mechanical, Electrical, and Electronics & Telecommunication —are eligible to apply for the ESE.

Is there a limit on the number of attempts for the ESE? No. Unlike the Civil Services Exam, there is no restriction on the number of attempts for the ESE. A candidate can appear for the exam any number of times as long as they satisfy the age-limit criteria.
❓ Regarding the Preliminary Exam

Is Paper I (GS & Engineering Aptitude) compulsory? Absolutely. You must appear for both papers of the Preliminary Exam. Paper I is a crucial component, and its score is added to Paper II's score to determine qualification for the Mains. A good score in Paper I is essential for clearing the Prelims cut-off.

Do the marks from the Preliminary Exam count towards the final merit list? No. The Preliminary Exam is purely a screening test. Your score in Prelims is only used to determine if you qualify for the Main Examination. The final rank is based solely on the marks from the Main Examination (Written) and the Personality Test (Interview).
Is there negative marking in Prelims? Yes. For every incorrect answer, one-third (1/3rd) of the marks assigned to that question are deducted. There is no penalty for unattempted questions.
❓ Regarding the Main Exam & Interview

Are scientific calculators allowed in the Main Examination? Yes. Candidates are permitted to use non-programmable scientific calculators for the Main Examination. This is a crucial tool for solving the complex numerical problems that are a major part of the descriptive papers.

Are there any language or essay papers in ESE Mains? No. The ESE Main Examination is purely technical. It consists of only two descriptive papers from your specific engineering discipline. There are no qualifying language papers or general essay papers.

What is the DAF (Detailed Application Form)? The DAF is a comprehensive form filled by candidates who qualify for the Mains. It contains details about your academic, personal, and professional background, including projects, hobbies, and service preferences. It is the primary source of information for the interview board.

How is the final rank determined? The final rank is based on the grand total of marks obtained in the Main Examination (Written - 600 marks) and the Personality Test (Interview - 200 marks) , out of a total of 800 marks. The merit list is prepared separately for each of the four engineering disciplines.

Institute of Banking Personnel Selection - Probationary Officer Exam
About the Examination

The Institute of Banking Personnel Selection (IBPS) Probationary Officer (PO) examination is a highly competitive, national-level recruitment process for the post of Probationary Officer/Management Trainee (Scale-I) in various Public Sector Banks (PSBs) across India. It serves as a unified gateway for graduates aspiring to a prestigious management-level career in the banking sector, offering immense growth opportunities, job security, and a chance to contribute to the nation's economy.
📜 The Philosophy Behind the Examination

The IBPS PO exam is designed to select candidates who possess the right blend of aptitude, knowledge, and personality for a dynamic and demanding banking career. It goes beyond testing theoretical knowledge and focuses on assessing practical skills essential for a modern banker.
Speed and Accuracy: The time-bound nature of the online exams, with strict sectional timings, tests a candidate's ability to solve complex problems quickly and accurately under immense pressure.

Analytical & Reasoning Skills: The exam evaluates logical thinking, problem-solving capabilities, and the ability to interpret complex data, which are crucial for making sound banking decisions related to credit, risk, and operations.

Language Proficiency: Strong command of the English language is assessed, as it is vital for customer interaction, internal communication, drafting official documents, and understanding policy circulars.

General & Banking Awareness: It tests a candidate's awareness of the economy, the banking industry, financial regulations, and current affairs, ensuring they are well-informed professionals capable of understanding the broader economic context of their work.
🏦 Participating Public Sector Banks

Successful candidates are provisionally allotted to one of the participating PSBs based on their rank and preferences. The initial pay scale for a PO (Scale-I) is approximately ₹36,000 - ₹63,840, with the gross salary being significantly higher due to allowances.
(List is subject to change as per vacancies reported by banks for a given year).
🪜 The Three-Tiered Selection Gauntlet
The IBPS PO selection is a rigorous, multi-stage process designed to meticulously filter candidates at each level.

Stage 1: Preliminary Examination (The Speed Test): An online objective test designed primarily to screen a large number of candidates. It tests fundamental skills in Reasoning, Quantitative Aptitude, and English within a highly constrained time limit. Marks from this stage are not considered for the final merit list; it is purely a qualifying hurdle to reach the main examination.

Stage 2: Main Examination (The Crucible of Knowledge): Candidates who clear the Prelims appear for the Main exam. This is a comprehensive online test comprising both objective and descriptive sections. It evaluates in-depth knowledge of reasoning, data interpretation, banking awareness, and English writing skills. The score from this stage is the most critical component for final selection.

Stage 3: Interview (The Final Appraisal): The final stage is a face-to-face interview conducted by panels of senior bankers and experts from participating banks. It assesses a candidate's communication skills, confidence, banking knowledge, problem-solving attitude, and overall suitability for the PO role.
🏆 The Final Verdict: Merit and Allotment

The final merit list is created based on the combined scores of the Main Examination and the Interview . The marks are normalized to a scale of 100, with a weightage of 80% for the Main Examination and 20% for the Interview . Based on the final score and vacancies, candidates are provisionally allotted to one of the participating banks.
Typical Timeline (Indicative)

The IBPS PO recruitment cycle is an annual process that is typically completed within 9-10 months. The schedule is fairly consistent year after year, with the final result being famously declared on the 1st of April.
⚠️ Disclaimer: These timelines are based on past trends. Always refer to the official IBPS notification for the specific year for exact dates.
Phase 1: Notification & Application (July - August)
Late July / Early August: The official detailed notification is released by IBPS on its website (ibps.in).
August: The online application window opens and remains active for about 20-22 days . Candidates must complete their registration and fee payment during this period.
Phase 2: Pre-Exam Training & Prelims Admit Card (September - October)
September: IBPS arranges Pre-Examination Training (PET) for candidates from SC/ST/Minority Communities at certain centres.
Late September / Early October: The call letters (Admit Cards) for the Preliminary Examination are released online for all registered candidates.
Phase 3: Preliminary Examination (October)
The online Preliminary Examination is conducted on multiple dates, usually over two weekends in October, to accommodate the large number of applicants.
Phase 4: Prelims Result & Mains Admit Card (November)
Early November: Results of the Preliminary Examination are declared, along with the scorecards and cut-offs.
Mid-November: Call letters for the Main Examination are released for candidates who have qualified in the Prelims.
Phase 5: Main Examination (November)
The online Main Examination (Objective + Descriptive) is conducted on a single day, typically in the last week of November.
Phase 6: Mains Result & Interview Call Letters (December - January)
December: The results of the Main Examination are announced, listing candidates shortlisted for the interview.
January: Shortlisted candidates can download their call letters for the Interview, which specify the date, time, and venue.
Phase 7: Interviews (January - February)
Interviews are conducted by the participating banks under the coordination of IBPS at select nodal centres across the country.
Phase 8: Final Result & Provisional Allotment (April)

1st April: IBPS declares the final combined result for the Main exam and Interview. A final merit list is published, and candidates are provisionally allotted to a bank based on their rank and preferences.
Eligibility Criteria
Candidates must fulfill the eligibility criteria prescribed by IBPS to apply for the PO examination. Eligibility is determined by Nationality, Age, and Educational Qualification.
⚠️ Note: The official notification for the current examination year is the final authority on eligibility criteria.
🌍 1. Nationality / Citizenship
🎂 2. Age Limit
The age is calculated as of a cut-off date mentioned in the notification (usually the 1st of the month of notification, e.g., 01.08.2025).
Minimum Age: 20 years
Maximum Age: 30 years
This means a candidate must have been born not earlier than 02.08.1995 and not later than 01.08.2005 (both dates inclusive), for the 2025 exam as an example.
🎓 3. Educational Qualification
The minimum educational requirement is as follows (as on the last date of online registration):
A Degree (Graduation) in any discipline from a University recognised by the Govt. of India or any equivalent qualification recognized as such by the Central Government.

The candidate must possess a valid Mark-sheet / Degree Certificate that he/ she is a graduate on the day he / she registers and indicate the percentage of marks obtained in Graduation while registering online.

Final-Year Students: Candidates in their final year/semester are generally not eligible unless their result is declared and they have the degree certificate/final mark sheet on or before the cut-off date specified in the notification.

Computer Literacy: Working knowledge of computer systems is mandatory. Candidates should have a Certificate/Diploma/Degree in computer operations/language or should have studied Computer / Information Technology as one of the subjects in High School/College/Institute.
Language Proficiency: Verbal and written proficiency in the official language of the State/UT is desirable.
✍️ 4. Number of Attempts
There is no limit on the number of attempts for the IBPS PO exam. Candidates can appear for the exam as many times as they wish, provided they meet the age and educational eligibility criteria.
Stages, Exam Pattern & Marking Scheme
The IBPS PO exam is conducted in three phases: Preliminary, Main, and Interview. A thorough understanding of the pattern, sectional timings, and marking scheme is vital for success.
🎯 Stage 1: Preliminary Examination (Online Objective)
This is a qualifying exam. Candidates must clear the sectional as well as the overall cut-off to be shortlisted for the Main exam.
Online Mode: The exam is conducted online on a computer.
Sectional Timing: There is a fixed time of 20 minutes for each section. Candidates cannot switch between sections before the time for the current section expires.
Negative Marking: For each incorrect answer, one-fourth (0.25) of the marks assigned to that question will be deducted as a penalty.
Qualifying Nature: Marks are not counted for the final merit list. The result is declared as 'Qualified' or 'Not Qualified'.
📝 Stage 2: Main Examination (Online Objective + Descriptive)
The marks obtained in the Main Examination are considered for shortlisting for the interview and for the final merit list.
This test is conducted immediately after the objective test on the same platform to assess writing skills.
Separate Timings: Both objective and descriptive tests have separate timings. All sections in the objective test also have individual sectional timings.
Negative Marking: Applicable for the objective test (0.25 marks deducted for each wrong answer).

Merit Calculation: Marks from both Objective and Descriptive tests are considered for shortlisting and final merit. The descriptive paper is only evaluated if the candidate clears the sectional cut-offs in the objective test.
🗣️ Stage 3: Interview
Candidates who clear the Mains cut-off (approximately 3 times the number of vacancies) are called for a face-to-face interview.
Maximum Marks: 100 Marks

Minimum Qualifying Marks: Candidates must score a minimum of 40% (35% for SC/ST/OBC/PWBD) to pass the interview stage. Failing to do so will disqualify them from the final selection, regardless of their Main exam score.
Qualities Assessed: The interview assesses personality, communication skills, presence of mind, clarity of thought, leadership potential, and general and banking awareness.
📊 Final Rank Calculation
The final merit list is prepared by giving a weightage of 80:20 to the Main Examination and the Interview, respectively.
Final Score = [ (Main Exam Score out of 225) * (80/225) ] + [ (Interview Score out of 100) * (20/100) ]
Application Workflow
The application process for IBPS PO is entirely online. Candidates must follow the steps carefully to avoid any errors.
📋 Stage 1: Pre-requisites for Applying Online
Before starting the application, candidates must have the following documents ready as per the specified format:
A valid personal Email ID and Mobile Number, which must be kept active until the final declaration of results.
Scanned copy of a recent passport-style colour Photograph (4.5cm × 3.5cm, 20-50 kb).
Scanned copy of Signature (on white paper with Black Ink, 10-20 kb).
Scanned copy of Left Thumb Impression (on white paper with black or blue ink, 20-50 kb).
A Hand Written Declaration (on white paper with black ink, in English only, 50-100 kb), with the text specified in the notification.
Details/documents for online payment of the requisite application fee.
✍️ Stage 2: Online Registration and Application
Visit the official IBPS website: Go to www.ibps.in and click on the link for "CRP PO/MT".

New Registration: Click on "CLICK HERE FOR NEW REGISTRATION" and enter your basic information (Name, Mobile No., and Email ID). A provisional Registration Number and Password will be generated and sent via SMS and Email.

Fill the Form: Log in with the registration number and password to fill in personal, academic, and communication details. Validate your details at each step by clicking the 'Validate your details' button and then 'Save & Next'.
Upload Documents: Upload the scanned copies of your Photograph, Signature, Left Thumb Impression, and Hand Written Declaration as per the specifications.
Bank Preferences: Candidates will be asked to indicate their preferences for participating banks in order of priority. This choice is crucial and cannot be changed later.
💳 Stage 3: Fee Payment
Application Fee (Indicative): ₹ 175/- for SC/ST/PWBD candidates. ₹ 850/- for all others (General/OBC/EWS).
₹ 175/- for SC/ST/PWBD candidates.
₹ 850/- for all others (General/OBC/EWS).
Payment Mode: The fee can only be paid online using Debit Cards (RuPay/Visa/MasterCard/Maestro), Credit Cards, Internet Banking, IMPS, or Mobile Wallets.
✅ Stage 4: Final Submission and Printout
After verifying all details and ensuring successful fee payment, click on the 'FINAL SUBMIT' button. No changes are possible after this.

Print Application: After submission, take a printout of the system-generated online application form and the e-receipt for the fee payment. These documents are mandatory to be produced during the interview.
⚠️ Common Mistakes to Avoid
Incorrect Specifications: Uploading documents that do not meet the size, dimension, and format requirements can lead to application rejection.

Handwritten Declaration: Do not type and print the declaration. It must be handwritten by the candidate in their own handwriting. Using all caps is not allowed, and the text must be exactly as prescribed.
Last-Minute Rush: The website may face heavy traffic on the last few days, leading to payment failures. Apply well in advance.
Syllabus
IBPS does not prescribe a detailed syllabus, but based on the analysis of previous years' papers, the important topics for each section are as follows.
The official notification from IBPS is the final authority on the exam pattern and scope of topics.

Reading Comprehension
Cloze Test
Fillers (Single, Double)
Para Jumbles / Sentence Rearrangement
Error Spotting / Sentence Correction
Vocabulary (Synonyms, Antonyms, Word Swap)
Idioms and Phrases
Match the Column
Data Interpretation (DI): Bar Graph, Line Chart, Tabular, Caselet, Pie Chart, Radar Graph
Speed Maths: Simplification & Approximation, Number Series (Missing, Wrong), Quadratic Equations

Arithmetic: Percentage, Ratio & Proportion, Profit & Loss, Simple & Compound Interest, Time & Work, Pipes & Cistern, Time, Speed & Distance, Boats & Streams, Averages, Problems on Ages, Partnership, Mixture & Allegation, Probability, Permutation & Combination

✒️ Part B: Main Examination Syllabus

Static GK: Important Days, Countries & Capitals, Currencies, Books & Authors, National Parks, Sports.

Frequently Asked Questions
❓ Regarding Eligibility & Application

Is there a minimum percentage required in graduation to apply for IBPS PO? No. IBPS does not prescribe a minimum percentage. A candidate only needs to have a passing degree from a recognized university. However, you must mention the correct percentage while filling the form.

What is the handwritten declaration? It is a text, specified in the official notification, that the candidate must write in their own handwriting, scan, and upload. The standard text is: “I, _______ (Name of the candidate), hereby declare that all the information submitted by me in the application form is correct, true and valid. I will present the supporting documents as and when required.” This text must not be written in CAPITAL LETTERS.

Can I edit my application after final submission? No. Once the application is finally submitted, no changes can be made. Therefore, it is crucial to fill in the details with extreme care and use the 'Save & Next' and 'Preview' options thoroughly before final submission.
❓ Regarding the Examination

Are there sectional cut-offs in the IBPS PO exam? Yes. Candidates must clear the cut-off for each section (sectional cut-off) as well as the overall cut-off in both the Preliminary and Main examinations to be shortlisted for the next stage.
Is the exam bilingual? Yes. All tests, except for the English Language test, are available in both English and Hindi.
❓ Regarding Selection & Allotment

Are the marks of the Preliminary exam considered for the final merit list? No. The Preliminary exam is only for screening/qualifying purposes. The final merit list is based on the combined scores of the Main Examination and the Interview.

How is the final allotment of banks done? The allotment is done based on the final merit list. A higher-ranked candidate gets their higher preference of the bank, subject to vacancy availability in their category. The process is strictly based on merit-cum-preference.

Institute of Banking Personnel Selection - Regional Rural Banks
About the Examination

The Institute of Banking Personnel Selection (IBPS) Common Recruitment Process (CRP) for Regional Rural Banks (RRBs) is a national-level banking exam conducted annually to recruit personnel for various posts in RRBs across India. This examination is a gateway for aspirants seeking a career in rural banking, which plays a crucial role in the economic development of rural areas.
📜 The Philosophy Behind the Examination

The IBPS RRB exam aims to select candidates who are not only proficient in banking knowledge but also have an aptitude for working in and understanding the rural economy. The core philosophy is to identify individuals who demonstrate:
Quantitative & Reasoning Skills: The ability to solve problems, analyze data, and think logically, which is essential for day-to-day banking operations.
Language Proficiency: Strong command over English and/or Hindi, along with knowledge of the local language of the state, is crucial for customer interaction.
General & Banking Awareness: A good understanding of the Indian economy, financial systems, current affairs, and computer literacy.
Commitment to Rural Service: A mindset geared towards contributing to financial inclusion and the development of India's rural sector.
🏛️ The Posts and Services at Stake
The IBPS RRB exam recruits for Group 'A' Officers and Group 'B' Office Assistants.
1. Group 'A' - Officers:
2. Group 'B' - Office Assistant:
🪜 The Multi-Stage Selection Process
The selection process varies depending on the post.

For Office Assistant (Multipurpose): This is a two-stage process. Preliminary Exam: An online screening test of Reasoning and Numerical Ability. It is qualifying in nature. Mains Exam: Candidates who clear the prelims appear for the mains exam. The final selection is based solely on the marks obtained in the Mains Exam . There is no interview.
Preliminary Exam: An online screening test of Reasoning and Numerical Ability. It is qualifying in nature.
Mains Exam: Candidates who clear the prelims appear for the mains exam. The final selection is based solely on the marks obtained in the Mains Exam . There is no interview.

For Officer Scale-I: This is a three-stage process. Preliminary Exam: An online screening test of Reasoning and Quantitative Aptitude, which is qualifying. Mains Exam: Shortlisted candidates appear for the mains exam. Marks from this stage are considered for final selection. Interview: Candidates who clear the mains exam are called for an interview. The final merit list is prepared based on the combined score of the Mains Exam and Interview.
Preliminary Exam: An online screening test of Reasoning and Quantitative Aptitude, which is qualifying.
Mains Exam: Shortlisted candidates appear for the mains exam. Marks from this stage are considered for final selection.
Interview: Candidates who clear the mains exam are called for an interview. The final merit list is prepared based on the combined score of the Mains Exam and Interview.

For Officer Scale-II & III: This is a two-stage process. Single Level Examination: A single online exam is conducted. There is no preliminary exam for these posts. Interview: Candidates qualifying in the single-level exam are shortlisted for an interview. The final merit list is based on the combined score of the exam and interview.
Single Level Examination: A single online exam is conducted. There is no preliminary exam for these posts.
Interview: Candidates qualifying in the single-level exam are shortlisted for an interview. The final merit list is based on the combined score of the exam and interview.
Typical Timeline (Indicative)
The IBPS RRB examination cycle typically spans about 7-8 months from notification to the final result. The following is a general, indicative schedule.
⚠️ Disclaimer: These timelines are based on past trends. Always refer to the official IBPS calendar and notification for the specific year for exact dates.
Phase 1: Notification & Application (June - July)
June: The official notification for RRB CRP is released by IBPS on its website (ibps.in). It details vacancies, eligibility, exam pattern, and application guidelines.
June - July: The online application and fee payment window typically remains open for about three weeks .
Phase 2: Preliminary Examination (August)
July / August: Approximately 10-15 days before the exam , IBPS releases the call letters (admit cards) for the Preliminary Examination for Officer Scale-I and Office Assistant posts.
August: The Preliminary online examinations are conducted over multiple weekends.
Phase 3: Mains & Single Level Examination (September - October)
September: Results for the Preliminary exams are announced.
September: Call letters for the Mains Exam (for Officer Scale I & Office Assistant) and Single Level Exam (for Officer Scale II & III) are released.
September / October: The Mains and Single Level online examinations are conducted, usually on separate dates.
Phase 4: Interview Process (November - December)
October / November: Results for the Mains/Single Level exams are declared, and a list of candidates shortlisted for interviews (for all Officer posts) is released.
November / December: Interviews for Officer Scale-I, II, and III are conducted by participating RRBs, coordinated by NABARD and IBPS.
Phase 5: Provisional Allotment (January of next year)
1st January: IBPS releases the final result and provisional allotment list for all posts. This list specifies the RRB allotted to successful candidates based on merit, preference, and vacancies.
Eligibility Criteria
Candidates must ensure they fulfill the IBPS RRB eligibility criteria, which are mandatory. Eligibility is determined by Nationality, Age Limit, and Educational Qualification.
⚠️ Note: The official IBPS notification for the current examination year is the ultimate authority on eligibility criteria.
🌍 1. Nationality

A candidate must be a citizen of India or a subject of Nepal/Bhutan, or a Tibetan Refugee who came to India before 1st January 1962, or a person of Indian origin who has migrated from specific countries with the intention of permanently settling in India.
🎂 2. Age Limit
The age is calculated as of a specific cut-off date, typically the 1st of June of the examination year. The age limits are:
For Officer Scale-III (Senior Manager): Above 21 years - Below 40 years.
For Officer Scale-II (Manager): Above 21 years - Below 32 years.
For Officer Scale-I (Assistant Manager): Above 18 years - Below 30 years.
For Office Assistant (Multipurpose): Between 18 years and 28 years.
🎓 3. Educational Qualification & Experience
Office Assistant (Multipurpose): Bachelor’s degree in any discipline from a recognized University. Proficiency in the local language as prescribed by the participating RRB is required.

Officer Scale-I (Assistant Manager): Bachelor’s degree in any discipline. Preference given to degrees in Agriculture, Horticulture, Forestry, Animal Husbandry, etc. Proficiency in the local language and working knowledge of computers is required.

Officer Scale-II (General Banking Officer): Bachelor’s degree in any discipline with a minimum of 50% marks in aggregate. Preference to specific degrees. Experience: Two years as an officer in a Bank or Financial Institution.

Officer Scale-II (Specialist Officers): IT Officer: Bachelor’s degree in Electronics/Communication/Computer Science/IT with 50% marks. Experience: One year in the relevant field. Chartered Accountant: Certified Associate (CA) from the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India. Experience: One year as a CA. Law Officer: Degree in Law with 50% marks. Experience: Two years as an advocate or should have worked as a Law Officer in Banks for a period of not less than two years.
IT Officer: Bachelor’s degree in Electronics/Communication/Computer Science/IT with 50% marks. Experience: One year in the relevant field.
Chartered Accountant: Certified Associate (CA) from the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India. Experience: One year as a CA.
Law Officer: Degree in Law with 50% marks. Experience: Two years as an advocate or should have worked as a Law Officer in Banks for a period of not less than two years.

Officer Scale-III (Senior Manager): Bachelor’s degree in any discipline with a minimum of 50% marks in aggregate. Preference to specific degrees/diplomas. Experience: Minimum 5 years’ experience as an Officer in a Bank or Financial Institution.
Note: A Language Proficiency Test (LPT) will be conducted for candidates who do not have the local language as a subject in their Class 8th or higher studies.
Stages, Exam Pattern & Marking Scheme
The IBPS RRB exam pattern varies for different posts. A key feature is the choice between English and Hindi in the Mains exam.
Common Features:
Mode: All exams are conducted online (Computer-Based Test).
Question Type: All questions are Objective Type (MCQs).
Negative Marking: For every wrong answer, one-fourth (0.25) of the marks assigned to that question will be deducted.
🎯 Office Assistant (Multipurpose) & Officer Scale-I
📝 Officer Scale-II & III (Single Level Examination)
📊 Final Selection
Office Assistant: Final selection is based on marks obtained in the Mains Examination.

Officer Scale-I, II, III: Final selection is based on the combined performance in the Mains/Single Level Examination and the Interview. The weightage ratio is typically 80:20 for the written test and interview, respectively.
Application Workflow
The application process for IBPS RRB is conducted entirely online through the official IBPS website (ibps.in) . Candidates must follow the steps carefully.
📝 Stage 1: Registration and Basic Information
New Registration: Click on the link for "CRP for RRBs" on the IBPS homepage and select "Click here for New Registration".
Enter Basic Info: Provide your name, mobile number, and email address. A provisional Registration Number and Password will be generated and sent via SMS and email.
Save and Next: Use these credentials to log in and proceed with the application.
✍️ Stage 2: Uploading Scanned Documents
This is a critical step. Candidates must scan and upload their photograph, signature, left thumb impression, and a handwritten declaration as per the specifications given in the notification.
Photograph: Recent colour passport-style photograph (4.5cm × 3.5cm). Size: 20kb–50 kb.

Handwritten Declaration: Written by the candidate in English on white paper with black ink. The text for the declaration is provided in the official notification. Size: 50kb–100 kb.
✅ Stage 3: Filling Details, Fee Payment, and Final Submission

Fill Application Form: Enter your personal, educational, and work experience details. Choose your examination centres and the RRB you wish to apply for, based on your state and local language proficiency.
Preview: Carefully check all the details entered in the application form before final submission.
Fee Payment: Amount: Application fees are typically ₹175 for SC/ST/PwBD candidates and ₹850 for all others. Mode: The fee must be paid online using a Debit Card, Credit Card, or Net Banking.
Amount: Application fees are typically ₹175 for SC/ST/PwBD candidates and ₹850 for all others.

Final Submit: After successful payment, a confirmation e-receipt and application form will be generated. Print and save both for future reference.
⚠️ Common Mistakes to Avoid
Applying to Multiple States: A candidate can apply for only one post (Office Assistant or Officer) and from only one state.
Incorrect Scanned Documents: Uploading documents that do not meet the specified format (size, dimensions, clarity) is a major reason for rejection. The signature should not be in capital letters.
Spelling Mistakes: Ensure your name and other details match exactly with your official documents (e.g., Aadhar, 10th marksheet).

Frequently Asked Questions
Here are answers to some common questions about the IBPS RRB Examination.
❓ Regarding Application & Posts

Can I apply for both Office Assistant and Officer Scale-I posts? Yes. You can apply for both posts. The applications need to be filled separately, and the fees paid for both. The exams are also conducted on different dates.

Do I need to know the local language of the state I am applying from? Yes. Proficiency in the local language specified for a state's RRB is mandatory. If you have not studied the language in 8th standard or above, you will have to pass a Language Proficiency Test (LPT) after selection.

Is there a bond period after joining an RRB? Yes. Most RRBs have a mandatory service bond for a specific period (e.g., 2-3 years). If you leave before the bond period ends, you will have to pay a penalty amount as specified in the appointment letter.
❓ Regarding the Examination

Is the IBPS RRB exam bilingual? Yes. All tests (except the English/Hindi language section) are available in both English and Hindi. Additionally, for some states, the questions are also available in the local language of that state.

Is there sectional timing in the IBPS RRB exams? No. Unlike IBPS PO/Clerk, the RRB Prelims and Mains exams have a composite time duration. You can switch between sections at any time within the overall time limit.

Are the scores of the Prelims exam considered for the final merit list? No. The Preliminary exam is only for screening/qualifying purposes. The final merit list is based on the Mains exam score (for Office Assistant) or the combined score of Mains and Interview (for Officers).
❓ Regarding Cut-offs & Selection
Are there both sectional and overall cut-offs? Yes. For all stages, you must clear the minimum cut-off score in each section as well as the overall cut-off to be shortlisted for the next stage.
Are the cut-offs state-wise? Yes. Since the vacancies are declared state-wise for each RRB, the cut-offs are also determined state-wise. They can vary significantly from one state to another.

What happens after the provisional allotment? After IBPS issues the provisional allotment, the respective Regional Rural Banks will contact you for document verification, medical examination, and other joining formalities. IBPS has no further role after the allotment.

Indian Space Research Organisation Recruitment
About the Examination
🚀 The Philosophy Behind the Examination

The selection process is designed to identify engineers with a strong foundation in their core discipline, exceptional problem-solving abilities, and a passion for innovation. ISRO seeks individuals who possess:
Deep Conceptual Clarity: A thorough understanding of fundamental engineering principles and their practical applications.
Analytical and Critical Thinking: The ability to analyze complex technical problems and devise logical, efficient solutions.
Passion for Space Technology: A genuine interest in and motivation for contributing to India's space missions.
Adaptability and Learning Agility: The potential to work in a dynamic, multi-disciplinary R&D environment and continuously learn new technologies.
🔬 Disciplines and Opportunities
ISRO conducts recruitment for the Scientist/Engineer 'SC' post across several engineering disciplines based on its requirements. The primary streams include:
Other specialized fields like Civil, Refrigeration & Air Conditioning, and Architecture are also recruited as per specific vacancies.
🪜 The Two-Stage Selection Process
The selection is a rigorous two-step process designed to filter for both theoretical knowledge and practical aptitude.

Stage 1: Written Test: This is an objective-type (MCQ) screening test focused entirely on the specific engineering discipline of the candidate. It is a comprehensive test of the core B.E./B.Tech curriculum. The primary role of this test is to shortlist a manageable number of candidates for the next stage.

Stage 2: Personal Interview: Candidates who clear the cut-off in the written test are called for a personal interview. This is a crucial and in-depth technical interview conducted by a panel of senior ISRO scientists and experts. It assesses the candidate's grasp of fundamental concepts, practical knowledge, and overall suitability for a research and development role.
🏆 The Final Merit: A Balanced Assessment

The final merit list is prepared with a balanced weightage given to both stages. The final selection is based on the combined scores of the Written Test and the Personal Interview . Typically, a 50:50 weightage is assigned to both, making the interview as important as the written exam for securing a position.
Typical Timeline (Indicative)

Unlike the fixed annual calendar of UPSC, the ISRO Scientist/Engineer 'SC' recruitment timeline is vacancy-driven and can be irregular . Notifications are released as and when vacancies arise in different centres. The following is a generalized timeline of events once a notification is published.
⚠️ Disclaimer: This is a hypothetical timeline. Always refer to the specific, official ISRO notification for exact dates.
Phase 1: Notification & Application (Variable, e.g., May - June)

Notification Release: The official notification is published on the ISRO Careers portal (isro.gov.in/careers) and in the Employment News. This document contains all crucial details: number of vacancies per discipline, eligibility criteria, age cut-off date, syllabus, and exam centers.
Application Window: The online application window typically remains open for about 20-25 days . Candidates must apply through the designated portal.
Phase 2: Scrutiny and Admit Card (e.g., July - August)
Application Scrutiny: ISRO scrutinizes applications to ensure they meet all eligibility criteria.

Admit Card Release: E-Admit Cards for the written test are made available for download on the ISRO portal, usually 2-3 weeks before the exam date . An email or SMS alert is typically sent to registered candidates.
Phase 3: Written Examination (e.g., September)
The Written Test is conducted on a single day across various centres in India. It is a computer-based test (CBT) or offline OMR-based test for the specific engineering discipline.
Phase 4: Written Test Results & Interview Call Letters (e.g., October - November)
Result Declaration: The results of the written test, along with the cut-off marks, are published on the ISRO website. A list of shortlisted candidates for the interview is released.
Interview Call Letters: Shortlisted candidates can download their call letters for the personal interview, which will specify the date, time, and venue (usually a major ISRO centre).
Phase 5: Personal Interviews (e.g., November - December)

Interviews are conducted in batches over several days or weeks, depending on the number of candidates. Candidates must attend in person at the designated ISRO centre. Document verification is also done at this stage.
Phase 6: Final Result Declaration (e.g., January)

The final merit list, based on the combined scores (50% from written test + 50% from interview), is published on the ISRO website. This list contains the names of the provisionally selected candidates.
Phase 7: Joining Formalities (e.g., February - March)

Selected candidates receive their offer letters and are required to complete pre-employment formalities, including medical fitness tests. The joining date and initial posting location are communicated, marking the start of their journey at ISRO.
Eligibility Criteria

Aspirants must strictly meet the eligibility criteria specified in the official notification. These are non-negotiable and are verified at the time of the interview. The key parameters are Nationality, Educational Qualification, and Age Limit.
⚠️ Note: Always verify the criteria from the specific recruitment notification, as cut-off dates and specific requirements can vary.
🌍 1. Nationality
The candidate must be a Citizen of India .
🎓 2. Educational Qualification
The minimum educational requirement is a first-class Bachelor's degree in Engineering/Technology.
A candidate must have a B.E./B.Tech or equivalent qualification in the relevant discipline from a recognized University/Institution.
Minimum Marks: An aggregate minimum of 65% marks or a CGPA of 6.84 on a 10-point scale is required. This is a mandatory, non-negotiable requirement for all candidates.

Final-Year Students: Candidates who are in their final year of B.E./B.Tech are also eligible to apply, provided they can produce their final degree certificate by the date specified in the notification and have secured the required aggregate percentage.
🎂 3. Age Limit
The age of a candidate is calculated as of the closing date of the online application mentioned in the notification.
Maximum Age (General/UR): 28 years .
ISRO provides relaxations in the upper age limit for candidates from reserved categories:
Note on Attempts: Unlike UPSC, there is no limit on the number of attempts for the ISRO examination, as long as the candidate meets the age and educational criteria.
Selection Process & Marking Scheme

The selection process for the Scientist/Engineer 'SC' post is a two-stage merit-based system. Each stage is designed to rigorously evaluate the candidate's technical prowess and suitability for a scientific role at ISRO.
🎯 Stage 1: Written Test (Objective Type)
This is the screening stage designed to test the depth of a candidate's knowledge in their specific engineering discipline.
Correct Answer: The marking scheme can vary slightly per notification, but a common pattern is +3 marks for each correct answer.
Incorrect Answer (Negative Marking): There is a penalty for wrong answers. Typically, -1 mark (or one-third of the marks for a correct answer) is deducted.
Unattempted Question: No marks are awarded or deducted.
Candidates are shortlisted for the interview in a ratio of approximately 1:5 (i.e., for every 1 vacancy, 5 candidates are called) based on their performance in the written test.
🗣️ Stage 2: Personal Interview

The final stage is a comprehensive technical interview conducted by a panel of senior ISRO scientists. It is a true test of a candidate's fundamental understanding and practical application of engineering concepts.
Maximum Marks: 100 Marks
Minimum Qualifying Marks: Candidates must score a minimum of 60 out of 100 marks in the interview to be considered for the final merit list.

Nature of Interview: It is highly technical and concept-driven. The panel probes the candidate's knowledge of core subjects, their final year project, and their ability to apply principles to solve real-world problems. The focus is on clarity of thought and depth of understanding, not rote memorization.
Qualities Assessed: The board evaluates fundamental knowledge, problem-solving skills, analytical ability, practical orientation, and passion for the field.
📊 Final Merit Calculation
The final selection is based on the aggregate score from both stages, with equal importance given to each.
50% Weightage from Written Test Score + 50% Weightage from Interview Score = Final Merit Score
The final merit list is generated based on this combined score, and candidates are selected in order of merit against the available vacancies for their discipline.
Application Workflow

The application process for the ISRO Scientist/Engineer 'SC' examination is conducted entirely online through the official ISRO or affiliated centre's portal. Candidates must ensure they have all necessary documents and details ready before starting the application.
🔍 Step 1: Find the Active Advertisement
Regularly check the ISRO Careers page for active recruitment notifications. Once a relevant advertisement (for your discipline) is found, read the notification document thoroughly before applying.
✍️ Step 2: Online Registration and Form Filling
Visit the Portal: Click on the application link provided in the advertisement.
Registration: Register on the portal using a valid email ID and mobile number. These will be used for all future communications.

Fill Application Form: Log in and fill in the online application form with accurate details, including: Personal information (Name, DOB, Category, etc.). 📂 Step 3: Uploading Documents
Candidates are required to upload scanned copies of their recent photograph and signature as per the specifications mentioned in the notification.
Scanned Photograph: A recent passport-size colour photograph with a light background (Format: JPG/JPEG, Size: typically under 50 KB).
Scanned Signature: Signature on white paper with a black pen (Format: JPG/JPEG, Size: typically under 50 KB).
💳 Step 4: Payment of Application Fee
Fee Amount: A non-refundable application fee, typically ₹250 (Rupees Two Hundred and Fifty only). However, initially, all candidates have to uniformly pay the processing fee.
Refund Policy: The processing fee is refunded to candidates who are exempted (Women, SC/ST, Ex-Servicemen, PwBD) and to others who appear for the written test.
Payment Modes: The fee can be paid online using Net Banking, Debit/Credit Cards, or UPI.
✅ Step 5: Final Submission and Printout

Submit: Once you are sure all details are correct, submit the application.

Printout: After successful submission and payment, a unique Registration Number is generated. Download and take a printout of the application form and the payment receipt for your records and future reference.
